details.body: Wad, s. cUrRaroDanI.
WAD: I Subs.: lozwam (?).II Verb: lozwayati (nomi: (?).
WAD , WADDING, s. AgneyacUrRaroDanavastu n., cUrRaroDanI, cUrRastamBanaM.
Waddle, v. i. haMsavat gam 1 P or car 1 P.
WADDLE: (1) Kelati (Kel, c. 1. = play);(2) carati (car, c. 1. = move). W.ing: haMsagati (mfn.) and sim. comp.s.
To WADDLE , v. n. haMsavat car or kram, haMsagatiH -tiH -ti BU.
WADDLE , WADDLING, s. haMsagatiH f., haMsavad gatiH f., vizamagatiH.
Wade, v. i. tF 1 P, kazwena gam 1 P, kfcCreRa pAraM gam.
WADE: kazwena gacCati (gam, c. 1. = to go: q. v.) or tarati (tF, c. 1. = cross: q. v.).
To WADE , v. n. duHKena pAdAByAM jale car or kram, kazwena pAdAByAM gADajale kram, duHKena pAdAByAM jalapAraM gam.
WAFER: no equiv.: vEBAram.
WAFER , s. (Thin cake) tanupizwakaH, sUkzmapizwakaH, SaktuPalakaH. — (For letters) vePar or vEPar must be used.
Waft, v. t. vah 1 P or c., utkF 6 P; kaRavAhI mAlinItaraMgARAM (S. 3); puzpareRUtkirErvAtEH (R. i. 38); (boat &c.) vah; praRud c., pracud 10, prer c.; See Drive. v. i. plu 1 A, vAyunA vah-nI pass.
WAFT: I To drive: q. v.: vAhayati (c. of vah). II To float: q. v.: plavate (plu, c. 1.).
To WAFT , v. a. SanEH SanEr vAyO or vAyunA vah (c. 10. vAhayati -yituM) or AnI, vAyunA prer or praRud or upanud.
To WAFT , v. n. SanEH SanEr vAyO or vAyunA vah in pass. (uhyate).
WAFTED , p. p. SanEr vAyupreritaH -tA -taM or upanunnaH -nnA -nnaM.
Wag, v. t. saM-, cal c., vi-, DU 5, 9 U, vikzip 6 P; ‘w(ag)ging the tail’ lAMgUlacAlanaM-vikzepaH-viDUti f. v. i. cal 1 P, DU pass. s. parihAsavAdin m. [Wag]gish, a. See Witty. Wag-tail, s. KaMjanaH.
WAG (v. t.): (1) cAlayati (c. of cal = move), w. ging of tail: lANgUlacAlanam, H. ii. 42.;(2) viDUnayati (DU, c. 10. = shake), by w.ging their tails: lANgUlaviDUnanEH, M. n. on Ku. i. 13.
WAG (v. i.): (1) calati (cal, c. 1. = move); (2) Duvati (DU, c. 6. = shake).
To WAG , v. a. itastataH saMcal (c. 10. -cAlayati -yituM) or cal.
To WAG , v. n. itastataH saMcal (c. 10. -calati -lituM) or vical or cal.
WAG , s. parihAsavedI m. (n), rasajYaH, vidUzakaH, DanvI m. (n).
WAG-TAIL , s. KaYjanaH -nikA, KaYjarIwaH, KaYjaKelaH, KaYjaKewaH, kaRAwIraH -rakaH, kaRAwInaH, BaRqakaH, gUQanIqaH, hAputrI, kAkaCadaH, kAkaCardiH m.
Wage, v. t. (War) vigrah 9 P, yudDaM AraB 1 A.
To WAGE , v. a. (War) vigrah (c. 9. -gfhlAti -grahItuM), vigrahaM kf.
Wager, s. glahaH, paRaH. v. glah-paR 1 A, (with gen. of thing staked).

WAGER: I Subs.:(1) paRaH, counter w.: pratipaRaH, Mah. ii. 60. 7.;(2) glahaH, description of different kinds of w. s: glahapraBedavarRanam, D. ii. II Verb.:(1) paRate (paR, c. 1.), one who has no property cannot w. another's property: asvo hyaSaktaH paRituM parasvam, Mah. ii. 67. 47.; (2) glahate (glah, c. 1.), Mah. ii. 61. 1.
WAGER , s. paRaH, AkzikapaRaH, nIviH -vI f., pratijYA.
To WAGER , v. a. paR (c. 1. paRate -RituM), vipaR. See To BET.
Wages, s. vetanaM, Bfti f., mUlyaM, nirveSaH, paRaH; See Hire.
WAGES: I Lit.: vetanam: v. Salary.II Fig.: mUlyam: v. Price.
WAGES , s. vetanaM, BftiH f., BAwiH f., BAwakaH, varttanaM. See HIRE.
Wagon, s. pravahaRaM, yAnaM, SakawaH-waM, cAturaM. [Wagon]er, s. SAkawikaH, SakawavAhaH, cAturikaH.
WAGON: pravahaRam: v. Cart, carriage.
WAGON , s. SakawaH -wI -waM, gantrI, gantrIraTaH, vAhanaM, cAturaM.
WAGONER , s. SAkawikaH, SakawavAhakaH, gantrIvAhakaH, cAturikaH.
WAGTAIL: a bird: (1) KaYjanaH;(2) KaYjaKelaH; (3) KaYjarIwaH.
Waif, s. ajYAtasvAmikaM dravyaM.
WAIF: aBijYAtasvAmikaM or asvAmikaM dravyam.
WAIL: Socati (Suc, c. 1.): v. To lament, bewail.
To WAIL , v. n. paridev, Akrand, vilap. See To LAMENT, MOAN.
WAILING (subs.): paridevanam: v. Lamentation, cry.
WAILING , s. paridevanaM, AkrandanaM. See LAMENTATION.
Wain, s. govahanaM, SakawaH-waM.
WAIN: govahanam: v. Cart, carriage.
WAIN , s. SakawaH -wI -waM, azwAgavaM. See WAGON.
Wainscot, s. BittipawalaM.
WAINSCOT: no equiv.: PalakinI may be used.
WAINSCOT , s. BittivahiHsTaM kAzWaPalakamayaM pawalaM, BittipawalaM.
Waist, s. maDyaH-DyaM, maDyamaH-maM, kawi-wI f., kawi-deSaH; ‘w(aist)-coat’ kawivastraM.
WAIST: maDya (mn.), having slender w.: kfSamaDya or tanumaDya (f. DyA), M. n. on Ku. i. 39.
WAIST , s. maDyaH -DyaM, maDyamaH -maM, maDyasTalaM, avalagnaH -gnaM, vilagnaH -gnaM, uddAnaM, kawideSaH, kawitawaM, kawiH -wI m. f.
WAIST-COAT , s. kawivastraM, maDyavastraM, maDyamavastraM, antarIyaM.
WAISTCOAT: no equiv.: uraScolaH may be used.

Wait, v. i. sTA 1 P; (for) prati-Ikz 1 A, anu-prati-pA c. (pAlayati) (of time and persons); ‘w(ait) for some time’ kAlaH kaScitpratIkzyatAM (K. ii. 54); mAM pratipAlaya &c.; sah 1 A, sTA, (of time only) (dvitrARyahAnyaharsi soQumarhan R. v. 25); sPuliMgAvasTayA vahnireDApekza iva sTitaH (S. 7) ‘here is fire in the state of a spark (only) w(ait)ing for fuel (to blaze up)’; (on or upon) upasTA 1 A, upa-anu-As 2 A, upa-sev 1 A, upa-car 1 P; ‘w(ait) at table’ pariviz c. [Wait]er, s. sevakaH, parivezakaH, parivezwf m., (at table).

WAIT (v.): (1) prati- Ikzate, apa- (Ikz, c. 1.), w. for a short time: kAlaH kaScit pratIkzyatAm, Ku. ii. 54.;(2) prati-pAlayati pari-, anu-, (pAl, c. 10.), where will you w. for me: kva punarmAM BavatyaH pratipAlayizyanti, V. i.;(3) tizWati (sTA, c. 1. = to stay: q. v.);(4) sahate (sah, c. 1. = bear up), w. for two months: sahasva mAsadvayam, D. i.

To WAIT , v. n. (Stay) sTA (c. 1. tizWati, sTAtuM), see To STAY, STOP. — (Wait for) pratIkz (c. 1. -Ikzate -kzituM), apekz, pratipAl (c. 10. -pAlayati -yituM), see To AWAIT, EXPECT; ‘one's arrival,’ Aga- manaM pratIkz; ‘wait a moment,’ kzaRaM tizWa, kzaRam apekzasva. — (Wait upon) upAs (c. 2. -Aste -situM), upacar, paricar, sev, upasTA, Sru in des., see To ATTEND; ‘at table,’ pariviz (c. 10. -vezayati -yituM), parivezaRaM kf.
WAIT , s. (To lie in wait) parAkramaRArTaM niBfte sTA.

WAIT ON or UPON: I To attend:(1) upa- tizWate (sTA, c. 1.), I will w. on the king: upa- sTAsyAmi rAjAnam, Mah. iv. 2. 1.;(2) upa-Aste, anu- (As, c. 2.), w. ed on by Arundhatī: anvAsitamarunDatyA, R. i. 56.;(3) upacarati (car, c. 1.);(4) sevate, upa-, (sev, c. 1.).II To await: q. v.
WAITER: I An attendant: parivezaka (f. zikA). II A tray: q. v.
WAITER , s. parivezakaH, parivezwA m. (zwf), paricaraH, sevakaH.
Waive, v. t. pari-tyaj 1 P; See Abandon.
WAIVE: tyajati, pari-, (tyaj, c. 1.): v. To relinquish, abandon.
To WAIVE , v. a. tyaj, parityaj. See To WAVE.
WAIVER: in law: AkzepaH: v. Abandonment.

Wake, v. t. pra-buD c., jAgf c. v. i. pra-vi-buD 4 A, jAgf 2 P. s. jAgaraRaM, jAgaraH, praboDaH-DanaM. 2 padavI; ‘follow in the w(ake) of’ padavIM pratipad 4 A; See Treadful, a. (lit.) rAtrijAgara, nidrAvimuKa, vinidra, unnidra; jAgarUka, dakza, avahita, sAvaDAna. [Wake]fulness, s. jAgaraH-raRaM, asvApaH, asvapnaH, anidrA, praboDaH, jAgradavasTA. 2 dakzatA, avaDAnaM, &c.
WAKE (subs.): I Lit.: jAgaraRam.II Track: padavI.
WAKE (v.): I Trans.: praboDayati (c. of buD): v. To awake, arouse.II Intrans.: buDyate, pra-, vi- (buD, c. 4.): v. To awake.
To WAKE , v. a. jAgf in caus., prabuD in caus., see To AWAKE.
To WAKE , v. n. jAgf (c. 2. jAgartti -garituM). See To AWAKE, v. n.
WAKEFUL: (1) jAgarUka (f. kA);(2) jAgaraRaSIla (f. lA); etc.

WAKEFUL , a. jAgaraRaSIlaH -lA -laM, jAgarUkaH -kA -kaM, jAgaraH -rA -raM, jAgarI -riRI &c., jAgaritA -trI -tf (tf), nidrAvimuKaH -KA -KaM, anidrASIlaH -lA -laM, anidraH -drA -draM, vinidraH &c., unnidraH &c., rAtrijAgaraH &c.
WAKEFULNESS: (1) jAgaraRam;(2) jAgaryA;(3) jAgarUkatvam, -tA; etc.

WAKEFULNESS , s. jAgaraRaSIlatA, jAgaraRaM, rAtrijAgaraRaM, jAgaryyA, jAgftiH f., jAgaraH, jAgradavasTA, jAgarUkatA, nidrAvimuKatA, nidrABAvaH, anidrA, asvapnaH, asvApaH, unnidratA, OnnidryaM, vinidratvaM, yoginidrA, praboDaH.
WAKING , s. jAgaraRaM, prajAgaraH, jAgaraH, praboDaH -DanaM.

Walk, v. i. (padByAM) car-cal-gam 1 P. pari-, kram 1 U, 4 P, pAdAByAM yA 2 P &c.; ‘w(alk) about’, ‘w(alk) to and fro’ parikram, itastataH Bram 1, 4 P; (for pleasure) vi-hf 1 P, ‘w(alk) away, %(walk)% off’ apas 1 P, apa-yA-kram-gam &c. [Walk]ing, s. pAdacAraH-gamanaM; ‘w(alking) about’ parikramaH-maRaM; ‘taking a w(alk)’ vihAraH, viharaRaM, (vAyusevanArTaM) parikramaRaM. 2 gamanAgamanasTAnaM, aDvagamArgaH. [Walk]er, s. pAdacArin, pA(pa)dagaH.
WALK (v.): pAdAByAM carati (car, c. 1.), gacCati (gam. c. 1.) or krAmati (kram, c. 1.): v. To go, to move. W. to and fro: parikrAmati.
WALK, WALKING (subs.): pAdacAraH: and sim. comp.s. W. about: parikramaH, -Ram, W. for amusement: vihAraH or viharaRam.

To WALK , v. n. (Go on the feet) pAdAByAM gam (c. 1. gacCati, gantuM) or yA (c. 2. yAti -tuM), pAdAByAM kram (c. 1. krAmati, c. 4. krAmyati, kramituM), pAdAByAM cal or car; ‘backwards and forwards,’ gama- nAgamanaM kf. — (Walk about, as for pleasure, &c.) parikram, vihf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM), parikramaM kf. — (Walk off), see To DECAMP.

WALK , WALKING, s. pAdagamanaM, pAdacAraH, pAdavrajanaM, pAdakramaRaM, kramaRaM, pAdAByAM gamanaM; ‘walking about,’ parikramaH; ‘for pleasure,’ vihAraH, viharaRaM. — (Place for walking) vihArasTAnaM, gamanAgamana- mArgaH, padagamArgaH.
WALKER: pAdacArin (f. RI) and sim. comp. s: v. Above.
WALKER , s. pAdacArI m. (n), pAdayAyI m., pAdagaH, padagaH.

Wall, s. Bitti f., kuqyaM; ‘enclosing w(all)’ prAkAraH, varaRaH, sAlaH, prAcIraM; ‘take the w(all) of’ agrasTAnaM A-sad c.; ‘go to the w(all)’ ava-sad 1 P, avasanna-ucCinna a. BU 1 P; ‘drive to the w(all)’ ava-sad c., ucCid 7 P. v. t. prAkAreRa A-vf 5 U.
WALL: I Of a house:(1) BittiH;(2) kfqyam. II An inclosing w.:(1) prAkAraH;(2) varaRaH; (3) sAlaH. Ph.: (a) to drive to the w.: avasAdayati (c. of sad); (b) to go to the w.: avasIdati (sad, c. 1.).
WALL (v.): prAkAreRa AvfRoti (vf, c. 5.): v. To surround.
WALL , s. (Of a house, &c.) BittiH f., BittikA, kuqyaM, kuqyakaM. — (A surrounding or inclosing wall) prAkAraH, prAcIraM, parisaraH, sAlaH. — (Wall of bones, rubbish, &c.) equkaM, EqukaM.
WALLED , a. prAkArIyaH -yA -yaM, prAkArAvftaH &c., prAcIrAvftaH &c.
Wallet, s. BastrA; kzudrakozaH.
WALLET: (1) goRI (= sack);(2) BastrA (= bag).
WALLET , s. sopakAradravyakozaH, sopakAradravyADAraH, kzudrakozaH.
Wallow, v. i. luW 6 P, luw 4 P; krIq 1 P.
WALLOW: (1) luWati (luW, c. 1. = roll);(2) krIqati (krIq, c. 1. = sport).
To WALLOW , v. n. paNke luW (c. 6. luWati -WituM) or praluW or krIq (c. 1. krIqati -qituM); ‘a pig that wallows in mire,’ paNkakrIqaH.
Walnut, s. akzowaH, akzowaM (fruit).
WALNUT: I The tree: akzowaH (also AKowaH). II The fruit: akzowam.
WALNUT , s. (Tree) akzowaH, AkzowaH, akzoqaH, pIluH m., kandarAlaH -lakaH, karparAlaH.
WALRUS: nakraH (?).
WALTZ (subs.): I A dance: pratilomAnu- lomatvam; *Avartanam.II A music: *Avartana- saNgItam.
WALTZ (v.): expr. by subs. and karoti.
WALTZ , s. vivarttanftyaM, vivarttananftyaM, parivarttananftyaM.
WAN: vivarRa (f. rRA): v. Pale, languid.
WAN , a. pARquH -RquH -Rqu, vivarRaH -rRA -rRaM, pARquvarRaH &c.
Wand, s. daMQaH, yazwi f.
WAND: (1) daRqaH;(2) yazwiH;(3) vetram.
WAND , s. daRqaH, vetraM, yazwiH m. f., vetrayazwiH; ‘of death,’ kAladaRqaH.
Wander, v. i. pari-, Bram 1, 4 P, aw 1 P, vi-car 1 P, pari-kram 1 U, 4 P; ‘w(ander) from’ BraMS 1 A, 4 P, cyu 1 A. [Wander]ing, s. pari-, BramaRaM-awanaM. [Wander]er, s. pari-BramakaH, Bramim m.

WANDER: (1) Bramati or BrAmyati, pari- (Bram, c. 1. and 4.), w. ed about the world: paribaBrAma medinIm, V. p.;(2) awati (aw, c. 1.), w.ing through forest again and again: awAwyamAno'- raRyAnIm, B. iv. 2.

To WANDER , v. n. Bram (c. 4. BrAmyati, BramituM), pariBram, aw (c. 1. awati -te -wituM), paryaw, vihf, vicar, parikram, pravraj, parigam, BramaRaM kf, see To ROVE, RAMBLE; ‘to wander from,’ see To STRAY.
WANDERER: (1) BramaRakArin (f. RI), pari-;(2) pariBrAmaka (f. mikA) etc.
WANDERER , s. BramaRakArI m. (n), BramI m., pariBramI m., vihArI m.
WANDERING , s. BramaRaM, pariBramaRaM, pravrajyA. See ROAMING.

Wane, v. i. pari-kzi 1 P or pass., hras 1 P; See Decay, Decline. s. kzayaH, hrAsaH. [Wan]ed, a. parikzIRa, kzIRakala, prAptakzaya, nizkala, kalASeza (caMdraH). [Wan]ing, a. kzayin, kzaya in comp.; ‘w(aning) period’ kzayakAlaH, kfzRapakzaH, bahulaH, tamisrapakzaH.
WANE (subs.): (1) hrAsaH;(2) kzayaH: v. Decrease, decay.
WANE (v.): (1) hasamupEti (i, c. 2.);(2) kzayaM gacCati (gam, c. 1.); etc.
To WANE , v. n. kzi in pass. (kzIyate), parikzi, prakzi, saMkzi, hras.
WANE , s. kzayaH, kzitiH f., parikzayaH, apakzayaH, hrAsaH, tejaHkzayaH, tejo- hrAsaH; ‘of the moon,’ indukzayaH, kfzRapakzaH, aparapakzaH.
WANED , p. p. kzIRaH -RA -RaM, kzIRakalaH -lA -laM, kalAkzIRaH &c., apakzIRaH &c., nizkalaH -lA -laM, prAptakzayaH -yA -yaM, jAtakzayaH &c., jAtahrAsaH -sA -saM; ‘a waned moon,’ kalASezaH.
WANING (adj.): (1) by comp., w. fortnight: kzayapakzaH, Ki. ii. 27.;(2) kzayin (f. RI);(3) hrAsagAmin (f. nI); etc.
WANNESS: vivarRatAH Paleness, languor.
WANNESS , s. pARqutA, vivarRatA, vEvarRyaM, kAlimA m. (n).

Want, v. apekz 1 A, A-, kAMkz 1 P, iz 6 P; gen. ex. by, kAryaM, prayojanaM, arTaH, kiM (with gen. of that which wants and instr. of thing wanted); ‘I do not w(ant) this house’ mamAnena gfheRa na kAryaM, na prayojanaM &c.; ‘why do you w(ant) to see her’ kiM tayA dfzwyA (S. 2). 2 Wish, q. v. 3 pari-, hA pass.; hIna, rahita, nir in comp.; Aryasya suvihitaprayogatayA na kimapi parihAsyate (S. 1) ‘nothing will be w(ant)ing’ &c.; ‘w(ant)ing in courage’ SOryahIna, nirvIrya, &c.; ‘he w(ant)s wisdom’ sa nirbudDiH, jYAnarahitaH. s. apekzA, prayojanaM, kAryaM, AkAMkzA. 2 aBAvaH, virahaH, aprApti f., rAhityaM, hInatA. 3 nyUnatA, UnatvaM, apacayaH. 4 dAridryaM, DanABAvaH, durgati f., kfcCraM; ‘come to or reduced to w(ant)’ dAridryopahata, BAgyakzayapIqitAM daSAM prapanna (Mr. 1). [Want]ing, a. Una, nyUna, vikala; See Deficient.

WANT (subs.): I Destitution, absence:(1) aBAvaH, w. of money: DanABAvaH;(2) rAhityaB;(3) rahitatA, tvam;(4) hInatA, tvam. N. B.(2) to(4) chiefly in comp.II Indigence, poverty: [Page753] q. v.: dAridryam.III Anything wanted: aBAvaH, to supply w. s: aBAvaM pUrayati.IV Need: prayojanam.

WANT (v.): I To be without: hIyate, pari- (pass. of hA), nothing is w.ing in you: Aryasya kimapi na parihAsyate, Sa. i.; w.ing in riches: DanahIna (f. nA): v. Devoid of.II To require, need:(1) apekzate (Ikz, c. 1.), that it would w. other visible illustrations: yenAnyatra dfzwa nidarSana- mapekzeta, S. i. 4.;(2) AkANkzati (kANkz, c. 1.), here it w. s apekzitum: atra upekzitumityAkAMNkzati, Kav. vii.III To long for, wish: q. v.: vfRoti or vfRute (vf, c. 5.), whatever she w. ed she found brought to her: yadeva vavre tadapaSyadAhftam, R. iii. 6.

To WANT , v. a. or n. (Be without) hInaH -nA -naM BU or as, see To LACK; ‘he wants wisdom,’ budDihInaH or nirbudDir asti. — (Have need of) AkAMkz (c. 1. -kAMkzati -kzituM), apekz (c. 1. -Ikzate -kzituM), see To NEED. — (Desire, wish) iz (c. 6. icCati, ezituM), AkAMkz, kAMkz, see To DESIRE. — (Be deficient) nyUnIBU. — (Be in poverty) daridrA (c. 2. daridrAti -drituM).

WANT , s. (Absence of any thing) aBAvaH, asamBavaH, avizayaH, virahaH, aprAptiH f., rAhityaM, rahitatvaM, SUnyatvaM, adarSanaM; ‘from want of rain,’ vfzweraBAvAt; ‘from want of food,’ AhAravirahAt; ‘want of money,’ DanABAvaH. — (Occasion for) prayojanaM, see NEED. — (Deficiency) nyUnatA. — (Indigence) dAridryaM, DanABAvaH, dravyABAvaH.
WANTING , a. nyUnaH -nA -naM, avidyamAnaH &c. See DEFICIENT.

Wanton, a. vilAsavat, vilAsin; ‘w(anton) sport’ vilasitaM See Playful. 2 aniyaMtrita, nirmaryAda, svecCApravftta, lola, (svaBAvalola); svErin, svecCAcArin; kAma in comp.; ‘a w(anton) woman’ puMScalI, svEriRI, baMDakI. 3 jYAnataH-kAmataH-kfta, boDapUrvaM kfta. 4 pracura, vipula. v. i. vilas 1 P, krIq 1 P, vi-Bram 1, 4 P. [Wanton]ly, adv. savilAsaM; niryaMtraRaM, svEraM, svecCayA, yaTAkAmaM; kAmataH. [Wanton]ness, s. vilAsaH, kAmacAraH; na kAmacAro mayi SaMkanIyaH ‘do not suspect me of w(antonness)’
WANTON (adj.): I Sportive: vilAsin (f. nI specially of men).II Unrestrained: aniya- ntrita (f. tA).III Luxuriant: pracura (f. rA).
WANTON (v.): vilasati (las, c. 1.), w. ed with her: tayA saha vilalAsa, H.

WANTON , a. (Frolicsome) vilAsI -sinI -si (n), vilAsavAn -vatI -vat (t), see PLAYFUL. — (Lascivious) kAmukaH -kA -kaM, kAmI &c., lAlI &c., see LUSTFUL; ‘a wanton woman,’ puMScalI, banDakI, lAlinI. — (Self-willed, unrestrained) svEraH -rI -raM, svErI &c., kAmacArI &c., svecCaH -cCA -cCaM.
To WANTON , v. n. vilas (c. 1. -lasati -situM), krIq. See To PLAY.
WANTONLY: I In gen.: savilAsam.II With- -out restraint: aniyantritam.
WANTONLY , adv. kAmukavat, vilAsena, svecCayA, yaTecCaM, yaTezwaM.
WANTONNESS: (1) vilAsaH;(2) vilAsitA: v. Also sportiveness.
WANTONNESS , s. kAmukatvaM, lIlA, vilAsaH, lAlityaM, svEritA.

War, Warfare, s. vigrahaH, saMprahAraH, vErAraMBaH, vEraM, saMgrAmaH, yudDaM, raRaM, (a particular battle); ‘w(ar)-cry’ siMhanAdaH, kzveqA; ‘w(ar)-horse’ vArakIraH. v. i. vigrah 9 P, yuD 4 A, kf with (s.). [War]-like, a. raRapriya, yuyutsu, yudDadurdama; raRotsuka, raRavIra-SUra; ‘w(ar) qualities’ kzAtraDarmAHkzatraDarmAH; ‘w(ar) tribe’ kzatriyajAtiH. 2 sAMgrAmika-sAmarika- (kI f.).

WAR (subs.): (1) saMgrAmaH;(2) samaraH;(3) raRam; (4) samprahAraH;(5) saMyugaH;(6) AjiH;(7) samparAyaH; (8) vigrahaH: v. Also battle. Ph.: w. cry.: (1) siMhanAdaH;(2) kzveqA or kzveqitam, -nAdaH; etc.
WAR (v.): (1) vigfhvAti (grah, c. 9.: lit. and fig.);(2) saMgrAmayati, -te (rare);(3) saMgrAmaM karoti, etc.: v. Also to fight.
WAR , s. vigrahaH, yudDaM, prayudDaM, saNgrAmaH, raRaM, saMyugaH, samparAyaH yakaM, BImaraH, rAwiH f., see BATTLE; ‘one skilled in it,’ sAMyugInaH.

To WAR , v. n. (Make war) vigrahaM kf, vigrah (c. 9. -gfhlAti -grahItuM), yudDaM kf, yuD (c. 4. yuDyate, yodDuM), saMgrAm (c. 10. -grAmayate -yituM), saMgrAmaM kf; ‘wishing to make war,’ sisaMgrAmayizuH -zuH -zu; ‘war-chariot,’ syandanaH; ‘war-cry,’ siMhanAdaH; ‘war-horse,’ yoDaharaH, see CHARGER; ‘war-dance,’ vIrajayantikA.
Warble, v. kUj 1 P, vi-ru 2 P.
WARBLE: kUjati (kUj, c. 1.): v. To sing.

Ward, s. rakzA. 2 rakzitaH puruzaH, ASritaH, rakzakADInaH, rakzyaH. 3 viBAgaH. v. t. vAr 10 or vf c., ni-prati-°, niruD 7 U, niras 4 U, ni-prati-ziD 1 P, prati-han 2 P, vyapa-Uh 1 U. [Ward]en, s. rakzakaH, rakzApuruzaH. [Ward]er, s. rakzakaH, dOvArikaH, dvAHsTaH.
WARD (subs.): I Custody, protection: q. v.: rakzA.II Opposed to guardian: perh. rakzito bAlaH.III Of a town etc.: viBAgaH. IV In fencing: apasAraRam.
WARD (v.): nivArayati (vf, c. 10.): v. To prevent, dispel.

To WARD , v. a. (Off) prativf (c. 10. -vArayati -yituM), nivf, pratihan (c. 2. -hanti -ntuM), pratikf, niruD, apasiD, pratiziD, vyapoh; ‘a blow,’ pratiGAtaM kf, paritrARaM kf, hastavAraRaM kf, hastaDAraRaM kf, paryyAptiM kf.
WARD , s. (Of a town) purArdDavistaraH. — (Custody) rakzA. — (One under a guardian) nATADInaH, bAlaH, SiSuH m., kiSoraH.
WARD-ROBE , s. vastrADAraH, vastraBARqaM. — (Clothes) vastrasamUhaH.
WARDEN: rakzaka (f. kzikA): v. Keeper, guard.
WARDEN , s. rakzakaH, nATaH, aDyakzaH, aDikArI m. (n), pAlaH.
WARDER: (1) rakzaka (f. kzikA = guard);(2) dOvArika (f. kI = gatekeeper: q. v.).
WARDER , s. dOvArikaH, dvArADyakzaH, rakzakaH, darSakaH, see DOOR-KEEPER.
Wardrobe, s. vAsAMsi (pl.); vastrasamUhaH. 2 vastrADAnaM-ADAraH.
WARDROBE: I A closet; vastrADAnam, and sim. comp. s.II Clothes: q. v.: vAsAMsi (n. pl.).
Ware, Wares, s. paRyaM, paRyadravyaM; ‘w(are)-house’ paRyAgAraM, paRyADAnaM, paRyaSAlA.
WARE, WARES: paRyam: v. Commodity, goods.
WARE , WARES, s. paRyaM, viwpaRyaM, dravyaM. See COMMODITY.
WAREHOUSE: *paRyADAnam, dravyaniDAnam and sim. comp.s.
WAREHOUSE , s. paRyaSAlA, paRyadravyaSAlA, vikreyadravyaSAlA.
WARFARE: yudDam: v. War, battle.
WARFARE , s. yudDaM, saNgrAmaH, vigrahaH. See WAR, BATTLE.
WARLIKE: I Disposed to war:(1) raRapriya (f. yA), yudDadurmada (f. dA) and sim. comp.s.; (2) yuyutsu (mfn. = desirous of w.).II Mili- -tary: q. v.: sAMgrAmika (f. kI).

WARLIKE , a. (Pertaining to war) sANgrAmikaH -kI -kaM, sAmarikaH &c., sAmparAyikaH &c. — (Disposed for war) raRapriyaH -yA -yaM, raRakAmI -minI &c., raRAsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, raRotsukaH -kA -kaM, raRaSUraH -rA -raM, raRavIraH &c., yuyutsuH -tsuH -tsu.

Warm, a. tapta, uzRa, caMqa, Garma in comp.; (fig.) tIkzRa, caMqa, sotsAha. 2 GarmArta, AtapAkrAMta; ‘grown w(arm)’ Angry, q. v. v. t. tap c., Izat tap; ‘w(arm) oneself’ (in the sun) sUryAtapaM sev 1 A, (sevayetpfzWato hyarkaM H. 2); ‘w(arm) oneself at the fire’ agnyAtapaM sev. [Warm]ly, adv. sotsAhaM, sasnehaM, uzRaM &c. [Warm]ness, [Warm]th, s. tApaH, uttApaH, uzman m.; ‘w(armth) of wealth’ vittozmA. 2 caMqatA, tIkzRatA. 3 utsAhaH; ‘w(armth) of affection’ snehAtiSayaH.
WARM (adj.): I Hot: q. v.: tapta (f. ptA).II Fig.: caRqa (f. RqA): v. Vehement, sharp. III Rich: q. v. Ph.: to be or feel w.: Garma- manuBavati.
WARM (v. t.): tApayati, -te, pra-, saM-, (c. of tap), w. yourself: svagAtrARi pratApayasva, P. iii. 19.: v. To heat.
WARM (v. i.): fig.: (1) dIpyate (dIp, c. 4.); (2) by adj.

WARM , a. uzRaH -zRA -zRaM, IzaduzRaH &c., caRqaH -RqA -RqaM, uccaRqaH &c., IzaccaRqaH &c., taptaH -ptA -ptaM, IzattaptaH &c., Garmma in comp., see HOT; ‘water,’ Garmmapayas n. — (Suffering from heat) GarmmArttaH -rttA -rttaM.
To WARM , v. a. Izat tap (c. 10. tApayati -yituM) or santap or pratap, kiYcit tap, IzaduzRIkf; ‘the feet,’ pAdO pratap; ‘to warm one's self at the fire,’ agnitApaM sev.
WARM-HEARTED: (1) saralahfdaya (f. yA);(2) sahfdaya (f. yA).
WARM-HEARTED , a. hfdayI -yiRI &c., hfdayAluH -luH -lu, snehI &c.
WARMED , p. p. IzattaptaH -ptA -ptaM, kiYcittaptaH &c., IzaduzRIkftaH &c.
WARMLY: I Lit.: uzRam.II Vehemently: caRqam.III Cordially: sAgraham.
WARMLY , adv. uzRaM, sopmaM, caRqaM, pracaRqaM, sasnehaM, snehena.
WARMTH: I Heat: q. v.: uttApaH.II Vehe- -mence: q. v.: caRqatA.II Zeal, enthusiasm: q. v.: utsAhaH.
WARMTH , WARMNESS, s. uzRatA, uzRaH, caRqatA, uzmaH, kozRatA, kozRaM, tApaH, IzattApaH, uttApaH, rOdraH -draM. See HEAT, HOTNESS.

Warn, v. t. (pUrvaM) pra-anu-buD c., upa-diS 6 P, anu-SAs 2 P. 2 sUc 10, nirdiS, vi-jYA c. (jYApayati); ‘I w(arn)ed him of the impending danger’ pratyAsannApadaM taM prAboDayaM; oft. by Beware, q. v.; avahito Bava yadApatpratyAsannA. [Warn]ing, s. praboDanaM, upadeSaH.
WARN: (1) satarkayati (nomi.: (?);(2) upadiSati (diS, c. 6. = advice).

To WARN , v. a. (Caution, admonish) pratyAdiS (c. 6. -diSati -dezwuM), sandiS, pradiS, upadiS, pUrvve prabuD in caus., cit in caus. (ceta- yati -yituM), see To CAUTION, &c. — (Apprise) vijYA in caus. (-jYApayati -yituM), sUc.
WARNED , p. p. pratyAdizwaH -zwA -zwaM, praboDitaH &c., vijYApitaH &c.
WARNING: (1) satarkaH (?);(2) upadeSaH (= advice: q. v.).
WARNING , s. pratyAdeSaH, praboDaH -DanaM, pUrvvaboDaH -DanaM, sandeSaH.
Warp, v. t. A-vft c., saMkuc 1 P; (fig.) kaluzIkf, duz c. (dUzayati). v. i. Avft 1 A, saMkuc pass.
WARP (subs.): tAnaH, V. d. i. I 24.
WARP (v.): I Trans.: Avartayati (c. of vft): v. To turn, bend, deprave.II Intrans.: Avartate (vft, c. 1.).
To WARP , v. a. sAcIkf, vakrIkf, kuYc (c. 10. kuYcayati -yituM), AkuYc, saMkuc (c. 1. -kocati -cituM), Akfz, saMhf.
To WARP , v. n. saMkuc or kuYc in pass., tUR. See To SHRINK, v. n.
Warrant, s. pramARaM, aDikAraH; (written) anujYA-aDikAra-patraM. v. t. pamARaM dA 3 U, pramARIkf 8 U, aDikf c.; See Sanction. [Warrant]ed, a. sapramARa, sADAra. [Warrant]y, s. pramARapatraM.
WARRANT (subs.): I Authority: kzamatA.II The writ: kzamatApatram (?).
WARRANT (v.): I To authorize: kzamatAM dadAti. II To justify: samarTayati (arTa, c. 1.).III To assure: q. v.
To WARRANT , v. a. pramARaM dA, aDikAraM or aDikAritvaM dA, sapramARaM -RAM kf, sapramARIkf, pramARIkf. See To SANCTION, AUTHORISE.
WARRANT , s. (Authority, sanction) aDikAritvaM, pramARaM, anujYA, ASrayaH. — (Writ) AjYApatraM, SAsanapatraM, anujYApatraM, aDikArapatraM.
WARRANTED , p. p. sapramARaH -RA -RaM, sASrayaH -yA -yaM, sADAraH &c.
WARRANTY: perh. pratyayapatram and sim. comp. s.
WARRANTY , s. nirdozapatraM, niSCidrapatraM, pramARapatraM.
Warren, s. SaSakanilayaH.
WARREN: (1) SaSakaBUmiH etc. (for rabbits: (?).
WARREN , s. SaSakAlayaH, SaSakasTAnaM, SaSakASrayaH.
Warrior, s. BawaH, yoDaH, yodDf m., vIraH, raTin m., vikrAMtaH; See Hero, Soldier; ‘w(arrior)s on the enemyʼs side’ pratiBawAH.
WARRIOR: (1) BawaH;(2) yoDaH;(3) yodDf (m.): v. Also hero.
WARRIOR , s. (Soldier) yodDA m. (dDf), yoDaH, yuyuDAnaH, prahArI m., see SOLDIER. — (Hero) BawaH, suBawaH, vIraH, raTI m., syandanArohaH, raRa- paRqitaH, vikrAntaH, jAjI m., jajaH, see HERO.
Wart, s. kiRaH, carmakIlaH-laM, aDimAMsaM.
WART: kiRaH (= scar, corn).
WART , s. carmmakIlaH -laM, kiRaH, mAMsANkuraH, aDimAMsaM.
Wary, a. sAvaDAna, apramatta, dakza; See Careful.
WARY: apramata (f. ttA): v. Cautious, careful.
WARY , a. sAvaDAnaH -nA -naM, vicakzaRaH -RA -RaM. See CAUTIOUS.

Wash, v. t. pra-, kzal 10, pra-mfj 2 P or c., nij 3 U, ava-nir-°, DAv 1 U, 10; ‘w(ash) the mouth (after meals)’ upaspfS 6 P. [Wash]ing, s. DAvanaM, pra-, kzAlanaM, mArjanaM, avasekaH, nirRekaH. 2 AlepaH, vi-pra-lepaH-panaM. [Wash]ed, a. prakzAlita, nirRikta, DOta, DAvita, mArjita &c. [Wash]y, a. jalaDarmaka. Washerman, s. rajakaH, DAvakaH, nirRejakaH, (rajakI, rajakavaDU f.).

WASH (v.): (1) DAvate or DAvayati (DAv, c. 1. and 10.), w. (his) feet: pAdO DAvasva, Mr. iii.; (2) kzAlayati, pra- (kzAl, c. 10.), w. ing in water: jalakzAlanam, K.; to w. out infamy: ayaSaH prakzAlayati, Mah.;(3) nenekti or nejayati, nir- (nij, c. 3. and 10.: rare).
WASH (subs.): I W.ing.:(1) DAvanam;(2) kzAlaRam, pra-;(3) nejanam nir-.II A lotion: lepaH, vi-, A-.III Marsh, fen: q. v.

To WASH , v. a. jalena DAv (c. 10. DAvayati -yituM) or praDAv, jalena mfj (c. 1. mArjati, c. 2. mArzwi -rzwuM) or sammfj or prakzal (c. 10. -kzAla- yati -yituM) or kzal, jalena SuD (c. 10. SoDayati -yituM) or nirRij (c. 3. -Renekti -RektuM) or pU, snA in caus. (snApayati, snapayati -yituM); ‘to wash the face,’ muKamArjanaM kf, muKaprakzAlanaM kf; ‘the feet,’ pAdO prakzal; ‘the hands,’ hastO prakzal; ‘to wash out the mouth,’ Acam, upaspfS, see To RINSE.
To WASH , v. n. snAnaM kf, aBizekaM kf, snA (c. 2. snAti -tuM), jalABizekaM kf.

WASH , s. (Act of washing) DAvanaM, prakzAlanaM, kzAlanaM, mArjanaM, snAnaM, aBizekaH, see WASHING. — (Sloppy food for pigs, &c.) ameDya- jalAdimiSritam ucCizwAnnaM or BuktocCizwaM or BuktasamujJitaM. — (Materials to smear over) lepaH, vilepaH, pralepaH, lepanaM.

WASHED , p. p. kzAlitaH -tA -taM, prakzAlitaH &c., mArjitaH -tA -taM, jala- mArjitaH &c., DAvitaH -tA -taM, DOtaH &c., nirDOtaH &c., nirRiktaH -ktA -ktaM, snApitaH &c., snapitaH &c., snAtaH -tA -taM; ‘by waves,’ utta- raNgaH -NgA -NgaM.
WASHERMAN: (1) rajakaH;(2) nejakaH, nir-, Y. ii. 141.;(3) vastraDAvakaH.
WASHERMAN , s. vastraDAvakaH, vastrarajakaH, rajakaH, vastranirRejakaH, nirRejakaH, vastranejakaH, vastramArjakaH, mArjaH, vastraprakzAlakaH, BasmakAraH, karmmakIlakaH.
WASHERWOMAN: (1) rajakI;(2) rajakavaDUH; etc.; v. Above.
WASHERWOMAN , s. vastraDAvakI, vastranirRejakI, vastrarajakI, rajakI.
WASHHAND BASIN: hastaDAvanaBAjanam, and sim. comp.s.
WASHHAND STAND: DAvanaBAjanADAraH, and sim. comp. s. (?).

WASHING , s. prakzAlanaM, kzAlanaM, DAvanaM, mArjanaM, nirRekaH, nirRejanaM, ava- nejanaM, snAnaM, aBizekaH, avasecanaM; ‘of clothes,’ vastrakzAlanaM, vastra- prakzAlanaM, vastramArjanaM; ‘of the feet,’ pAdaprakzAlanaM, pAdayoH kzAlanaM, pAdaDAvanaM, pAdAvasecanaM, pAdAvanejanaM.
WASHY , a. jalaguRakaH -kA -kaM, atidravaguRakaH &c., atidravarUpaH &c.
Wasp, s. varawA, gaMDolI. [Wasp]ish, a. karkaSasvaBAva, varawASIla.
WASP: (1) varawA;(2) ganDolI.
WASP , s. varawA -wI, varawaH, ganDolI, ganDAlI, BramarakIwaH, varalaH, varolaH, vareRaH, vAralA, BfNgaH, BfNgarolaH, vizaSUka, vizaSfNgI, brAhmaRI, tElAwI, tfRazawpadaH, peSaskft m., iqAcikA.
WASPISH , a. karkaSaH -SA -SaM, SIGrakozI -pinI &c., varawaSIlaH &c.

Waste, v. t. kzi 1, 5 P or c., ava-sad c., naS c., kzE c. (kzapayati), hrAsaM-kzayaM-nI 1 P, apa-ci 5 U, vyay 10 (vyayayati). 2 (Away) muDA-vyarTaM-hf 1 P or gam c., vi-kzip 6 P. v. i. pari-, kzi, parihA, apaci pass., kzayaM-nASaM-layaM yA 2 P or gam 1 P, vinaS 4 P, avasad 1 P, hras 1 P; kzE 1 P; (in strength) aMgEH parihA pass.; See Lean. s. kzayaH, nASaH, apacayaH, vyayaH, hrAsaH, avasAdaH. 2 apavyayaH, vi-, kzepaH, haraRaM; ‘w(aste) of time’ kAlakzepaH-nASaH-haraRaM-yApanaM ‘w(aste) of breath’ vAgvyayaH-kzepaH. 3 (Land) KilaM, -BUmi f., maruBUH. a. ucCizwa, niHsAra, nirguRa. 2 nirjana, SUnya, Kila, aprahata, jaMgala; ‘lay w(aste)’ upa-plu 1 A, upa-dru 1 P, bAD 1 A, pIq 10. [Wast]ed, a. pari-, kzIRa, kzAma, apacita, &c. [Waste]ful, a. apavyayin, vfTAvyayin, vyayaSIla. [Wast]ing, a. kzIyamARa, kzayin. Wastepipe, s. ucCizwajalanAlI, pari(rI)vAhaH.

WASTE (v. t.): I To wear, impair:(1) kziRoti, pari-, ava-, pra-, saM- (kzi, c. 5.), without w. ing the body: tanumakziRvan, M. ii. 100.; he is to be w. d.: parikzIyata evAsO, H. ii. 95.;(2) avacinoti (ci, c. 5.), if (it) is afterwards w. d.: arvAk cedapacIyate, Mit.II To ruin, des- -troy: q. v.: kziRoti, it does not w. the reputa- tion of warriors: na tadyaSaH SastraBftAM kziRoti, R. ii. 40.III To squander: q. v.: kzapayati (c. of kzi), when the night was w. d: aTa kzIRAyAM kzapAyAm, K.: v. To pass, spend, throw away.
WASTE (v. i.): (1) kzIyate (pass. of kzi);(2) apacIyate, (pass. of ci);(3) kzayaM yAti (yA, c. 2.); etc., it gradually w.s: stokaM stokaM kzayaM yAti, Mr. x. 2.

WASTE (subs.): I In gen.:(1) kzayaH, in the case of immoveables shall be made to pay the w.: sTAvarasya kzayaM dApyaH, N. s.;(2) apacayaH, increase and w.: upacayApacayO, Mit.;(3) apavyayaH (= squandering);(4) kzepaH (= throwing away).II W. land:(1) Kilam, cultivation of w.: KilakarzaRam, Viv.;(2) KilaBUmiH and sim. comp. s.
WASTE (adj.): Of lands: (land) that lies w. for one year is half-w.: ekavarzapatitamarDaKilam, Viv.: v. Waste (subs.: II.). II Desolate, empty, desert: q. v.

To WASTE , v. a. vyayIkf, vyay (c. 1. vyayati, c. 10. vyayayati -yituM, rt. i), kzi (c. 1. kzayati, c. 5. kziRoti, c. 10. kzapayati, kzayayati -yituM), upakzi, kzayaM kf, kzIRIkf, vikzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM), niHkzip, kzip, naS (c. 10. nASayati -yituM), nASaM kf; ‘to waste time,’ kAlakzepaM kf, kAlaharaRaM kf, kAlakzayaM kf, kAlaM kzip.

To WASTE , v. n. kzi in pass. (kzIyate), parikzi, apaci in pass. (-cIyate), sad (c. 1. sIdati, sattuM), hras (c. 1. hrasate -situM), parihA in pass. (-hIyate), prahA in pass., kzO (c. 1. kzAyati, kzAtuM), kzIRIBU, naS (c. 4. naSyati).

WASTE , WASTED, a. or p. p. (Expended uselessly) apacitaH -tA -taM, vyayitaH &c., vyayIkftaH &c., vyayIBUtaH &c. — (Diminished) kzIRaH -RA -RaM, parikzIRaH &c., kzayitaH -tA -taM, kzAmaH -mA -maM, viSIrRaH &c.; ‘wasted with hunger,’ kzutkzAmaH -mA -maM. — (Refuse) ucCizwaH -zwA -zwaM, niHsAraH -rA -raM. — (As land) KilaH -lA -laM, jaNgalaH -lA -laM, jANgalaH -lI -laM, SUnyaH -nyA -nyaM, aprahataH -tA -taM. — (To lay waste) upadru, upaplavaM kf, vAD, pIq, see To RAVAGE.

WASTE , s. kzayaH, parikzayaH, upakzayaH, avakzayaH, kziyA, kzitiH f., apacayaH, vyayaH, apavyayaH, nASaH, kzepaH, vikzepaH; ‘of time,’ kAlakzepaH, kAla- kzayaH, kAlanASaH, kAlaharaRaM, kAlayApaH -panaM, kAlavyayaH; ‘of breath,’ vAgvyayaH, vAkkzepaH, vAkkzayaH. — (Desert ground) jaNgalaM, jaNgala- BUmiH f., SUnyaM, see DESERT.
WASTE-PIPE: (1) pari(rI)vAhaH;(2) ucCizwajala- nAlI.
WASTE-PIPE , s. parIvAhaH, parivAhaH, ucCizwajalamArgaH.
WASTEFUL: (1) apavyayin (f. nI);(2) vfTAvya- yin (f. nI); etc.: v. Prodigal.
WASTEFUL , a. vyayaSIlaH -lA -laM, arTaGnaH -GnI -GnaM. See PRODIGAL.
WASTING , part. kzIyamARaH -RA -RaM, apacIyamAnaH &c., kzayI -yiRI &c.

Watch, v. rakz 1 P, prati-, pA c. (pAlayati); See Protect. 2 nirUp 10, nirIkz 1 A, avekz. 3 upAs 2 A, upasTA 1 A; ‘w(atch) over’ aDi-zWA 1 P. v. i. jAgf 2 P, (fig. also), rakzArTaM jAgf. 2 ava-DA 3 U. avahita-sAvaDAna a. BU; ‘w(atch) for’ apekz, pratIkz. s. rakzA, nirUpaRaM. 2 rakzin m., rakzApuruzaH, rakzitf m. 3 jAgaraRaM, jAgarUkatvaM, dakzatA. 4 praharaH, yAmaH; ‘w(atch)-house’ ud-GAwaH; ‘w(atch)-man’ rakzin m.; rakzakaH; praharin m.; vEboDikaH, vEtAlikaH; ‘w(atch)-word’ pratyayavAc f. [Watch]ful, a. jAgarUka, dakza, sAvaDAna, apramatta. 2 prajAgara in comp., unnidra.
WATCH (subs.): I Keeping awake: jAgaraRam. II Protection: q. v.: rakzA.III Guard: q. v.: rakzin (m.).IV Of time:(1) praharaH; (2) yAmaH.V A time-piece: kAlamApaH.
WATCH (v.): I To observe: avaDatte (DA, c. 3.).II To tend, wait on: q. v.: upAste (As, c. 2.).III To guard, protect: rakzati (rakz, c. 1.).
WATCH (v. i.): I To be awake: jAgarti (jAgf, c. 2.: lit. and fig.).II To wait: q. v.: pratIkzate (Ikz, c. 1.). To w. over: paryavekzate (Ikz, c. 1.): v. To look into.

WATCH , s. (Guard) rakzA, rakzaRaM. — (Person watching) rakzakaH, rakzI m. (n), rakzitA m. (tf); ‘body of watchmen,’ rakzakaja- nAH m. pl., rakzakagaRaH, rakzigaRaH. — (Eighth part of the day, or three hours) praharaH, yAmaH; ‘last watch of the night,’ apara- rAtraH. — (Small time-piece) kAlamApanI, kAlamApanayantraM.

To WATCH , v. n. (Keep awake) jAgf (c. 2. jAgartti, jAgarituM), jAgaraRaM kf. — (Keep guard) rakzAM kf, rakzArTaM jAgf. — (Watch for) apekz (c. 1. -Ikzate -kzituM), pratIkz. — (Be vigilant) sAvaDAnaH -nA -naM BU or sTA, sacetanaH -nA -naM sTA.
To WATCH , v. a. (Guard) rakz (c. 1. rakzati -kzituM), pAl (c. 10. pAla- yati -yituM), paripAl. — (Observe) nirUp, nirIkz, vIkz, avekza. — (Watch over) aDizWA (c. 1. -tizWati -zWAtuM).
WATCH-HOUSE, WATCH-BOX: (1) udGAwaH (?); (2) piWaram (?).
WATCH-HOUSE , WATCH-BOX, s. udGAwaH, piWaraM. See GUARD-ROOM.
WATCH-MAKER: kAlamApakAra (f. rI) and sim. comp.s.
WATCHED , p. p. rakzitaH -tA -taM, aBirakzitaH &c., nirUpitaH &c.
WATCHFUL: I Of men: v. Wakeful.II Of nights etc.: jAgara- or prajAgara- in comp.
WATCHFUL , a. jAgaraH -rA -raM, prajAgaraH &c., jAgarI -riRI &c., jAga- rUkaH -kA -kaM, prabudDaH -dDA -dDaM, sAvaDAnaH -nA -naM, apramAdI -dinI &c., apekzI -kziRI &c. See VIGILANT.
WATCHFULLY: (1) sajAgaram: v. Also care- -fully, cautiously.
WATCHING , s. jAgaraRaM, jAgaryyA, jAgarttiH f., jAgriyA, nirUpaRaM; [Page836-a+ 51] ‘alternate watching and sleeping,’ upaSAyaH, viSAyaH.
WATCHMAKER , s. kAlamApanakAraH, kAlamApanavikrayI m. (n).
WATCHMAN: (1) rakzin (f. RI), A-;(2) rakzaka (f. kzikA);(3) praharin (f. RI).
WATCHMAN , s. rakzakaH, gfhABipAlI m. (n), gfhapAlakaH, ArakzakaH, praharI m. (n), arTikaH; ‘who announces the hours,’ vEboDikaH, vEtAlikaH.
WATCHWORD: perh. pratyayavAc (f.): v. Also signal.
WATCHWORD , s. samBAzA -zaRaM, raRasamBAzA, saMvid f., raRasaMvid.

Water, s. jalaM, aMbu-aMBas n., udakaM, vAri; payas n., toyaM, salilaM, nIraM, pAnIyaM, vAr f., ap f. (pl.) pATas n.; ‘land and w(ater)’ sTalajale ‘place where w(ater) is distributed’ prapA, pAnIyaSAlikA; ‘by w(ater)’ jalena, jalavartmanA; ‘of first w(ater)’ anarGya; ‘it can hold w(ater)’ pramARakowiM pravazwumarhati. 2 mUtraM, prasrAvaH; ‘make w(ater)’ mUtrotsargaM kf; ‘w(ater)-carrier’ jalavAhaH, udavAhaH, dftihAraH; ‘w(ater)-closet’ SOcakUpaH; ‘w(ater)-course’ jalamArgaH, pari(rI)vAhaH; ‘w(ater)fall’ jalaprapAtaH, nirJaraH; ‘w(ater)ing place’ prapA; ‘w(ater)-man’ nAvikaH, udavAhaH; ‘w(ater)melon’ goquMbaM, sewu n., taraMbujaM, kAliMgaM; ‘w(ater)mill’ jalacAlyacakraM, jalayaMtraM, ‘w(ater)pot’ GawaH, kuMBaH, kalasaH-SaH; See Jar; ‘w(ater)proof’ jalABedya; ‘w(ater)-snake’ jalasarpaH; rAjilaH; ‘w(ater)-spout’ jalavajraH; ‘w(ater)-wheel’ GawIyaMtraM, udaMcanayaMtraM. v. t. (jalena) sic 6 P, plu c., ukz 1 P. 2 jalaM pA c. or dA 3 U. v. i. jalaM muc 6 P or snu c. or pat c.; ‘my eyes are w(ater)ing’ jalalavasyaMdinI netre. 2 lAlAyate (D.). [Water]ed, a. jalaBUyizWa, anUpa; jalasikta; ‘w(atered) by rivers’ nadImAtfka; ‘w(atered) by rain’ devamAtfka. [Water]y, a. jalamaya (yI f.), jalAtmaka, jalarUpa; ‘w(atery) shafts’ varzaSarAH, DArASarasaMpAtAH. 2 jalAQya, bahUdaka, jalaBUyizWa, anUpa, jalaprAya.

WATER (subs.): Lit.: (1) jalam, cool w.-drink- ing: SItalajalapAnam; rain-w.: vfzwijalam; sea-w.: sAmudraM jalam; how to purify bad w.: duzwajalasya nirdozIkaraRopAyaH, Bha.;(2) vAri (n.);(3) ambu (n.);(4) salilam;(5) ApaH (f. pl.);(6) udakam; (7) amBas (n.);(8) payas (n.);(9) toyam; (10) nIram;(11) pAnIyam. Ph.: by land and [Page755] w.: sTalena ca jalena ca; it will not hold w.: tadapi pramARakowiM pravezwumizwe, D. s. l.; first w.: anarGeyo maRiH (?), V. m. 82. 5.II Urine: q. v.: prasrAvaH, to make w.: prasrAvaM or mUtraM karoti, An.

WATER (v. t.): I To wet with w.: (jalena, salilena, etc.) siYcati, aBi-, pra-, (sic, c. 6.), is w. ing the Mādhavi plant: mADavIlatAM siYcati, Sa. i.; richly w. ed with tears: ApyAyitA netrajalaprasekEH, B. xi. 5.; these trees have been w. ed: udakaM lamBitA ete vfkzAH, Sa. i.II To give w.: jalam etc. pAyayati (c. of pA); he w. ed the horses: hayAn pAyayAmAsa vAri saH, Mah. vii. 100. 15.; place for w. ing horse: aSvAnAmudapAnam, Mah. vii. 99. 58.
WATER (v. i.): I Of the eyes: vAri muYcati (muc, c. 6.).II Of the mouth: lAlAyate (nomi.).

WATER , s. jalaM, vAri n., ambu n., amBas n., salilaM, udakaM, udaM, payas n., toyaM, pAnIyaM, ApaH f. pl. (ap), nIraM, vAr f. n., pATas n., kIlAlaM, puzkaraM, arRas n., peyaM, salaM, saMvaraM, SaMvaraM, sambaM -mbaraM, savaM -varaH, kzIraM, pAyaM, kzaraM, kamalaM, komalaM, pIvA, amftaM, jIvanaM, jIva- nIyaM, BuvanaM, vanaM, kabanDaM, kaM, anDaM, sarvatomuKaM, meGapuzpaM, GanarasaH, vahnimArakaM, dahanArAtiH m., nIcagaM, kulInasaM, kftsnaM, kfpIwaM, pAvanaM, SaralakaM, tfzAhaM; ‘warm water,’ uzRodakaM, GarmmodakaM, GarmmAmbu n.; ‘cold water,’ SItodakaM; ‘boiling water,’ pakvavAri n., taptajalaM, taptodakaM, haraRaM; ‘land and water,’ sTalajalaM; ‘place where water is distributed,’ prapA; ‘holy water for the feet,’ pAdyaM, pAdodakaM, caraRodakaM; ‘bread and water,’ annodakaM; ‘grow- ing in water,’ jalodBavaH -vA -vaM, jalaBUH -BUH -Bu; ‘living on water,’ abBakzaH -kzA -kzaM; ‘living in water,’ jalacaraH -rA -raM, jalacArI -riRI &c.; ‘water-animal,’ jalajantuH m.; ‘having much water,’ bahUdakaH -kA -kaM; ‘having clean water,’ acCodaH -dA -daM, see OCEAN.
To WATER , v. a. (Irrigate) sic, ukz, see To IRRIGATE. — (Supply with water) jalaM dA, jalaM pA in caus. (pAyayati -yituM), jaladAnaM kf.
To WATER , v. n. (As the mouth, eyes, &c.) jalaM sru (c. 10. srAva- yati -yituM) or pat in caus.; ‘the mouth waters,’ utsukAyate.
WATER-CARRIER: (1) jalavAhakaH;(2) udavAhaH, and sim. comp. s.
WATER-CARRIER , s. udakavAhaH, udavAhaH, ambuvAhaH, dftihAraH -rI m. (n).
WATER-CLOCK: kapAlayantram, Su. xiii. 23.
WATER-CLOSET: *SOcakozWaH.
WATER-CLOSET , s. pAyukzAlanaveSma n. (n), SOcakUpaH.
WATER-COURSE , s. jalamArgaH, jalavAhanI, udakamArgaH. See DRAIN.
WATER-CRESS: SAkaBedaH.
WATER-FOWL, WATER-HEN: jalakukkuwaH (f. wI).
WATER-FOWL , s. jalakukkuwaH, jalavihaNgamaH, goraNkuH m., rAjaBawwikA.
WATER-LILY: kamalam: v. Lotus.
WATER-LILY , s. utpalaM, padmaH, jalakamalaM. See LOTUS.
WATER-MAN , s. potavAhaH, nAvikaH, potabaRik m. (j), GawikaH.
WATER-MELON: I The fruit:(1) goqumbam; (2) sewu (n.); tarambujam.II The plant:(1) goqumbaH;(2) sewuH.
WATER-MELON , s. tarambujaM, vfhadgolaM.
WATER-MILL: jalaprARaM cakram, jalacalacakram. etc.
WATER-MILL , s. jalayantraM, jalacakraM, udakayantraM.
WATER-POT: (1) GawaH;(2) kamaRqaluH;(3) kalasaH (large w.).
WATER-POT , s. GawaH, kalaSaH, kalasaH, jalakalaSaH, jalADArakalaSaH, udakapAtraM, udapAtraM, udakumBaH, nipaH, kuwaH, aluH f., AluH f.; ‘of a religious student,’ kamaRqaluH -lu m. n., kuRqI -RqikA.
WATER-SNAKE: (1) jalavyAlaH;(2) jalasarpaH; etc.
WATER-SNAKE , s. jalavyAlaH, jalaBujaNgaH, jalasarpaH.
WATER-SPOUT , s. jalavajraH, udavajraH, udakavajraH.
WATER-WHEEL , s. (For raising water) GawIyantraM, vilomaM.
WATER-WORK , s. jalayantraM, udayantraM, udakayantraM.
WATERED: well w.: jalaBUyizWa (f. zWA) and sim. comp. s; w. by rivers: nadImAtfka (f. kA).
WATERED , p. p. siktaH -ktA -ktaM, jalasiktaH &c., salilasiktaH &c.; ‘well watered,’ jalaprAyaH -yA -yaM; ‘by rivers,’ nadImAtfkaH -kA -kaM; ‘by rain,’ devamAtfkaH &c.
WATERFALL: (1) prapAtaH;(2) jalaprapAtaH.
WATERFALL , s. nirJaraH, JaraH, vAripravAhaH, saraH -rI, -JA, jalanirgamaH.
WATERING , s. sekaH, secanaM, siYcanaM, nizekaH, avasekaH -secanaM.
WATERING-PLACE: I Lit.: prapA.II A sana- -torium: jalasevanam (nI).
WATERING-PLACE , s. jalapAnasTAnaM, udakapAnasTAnaM, prapA.
WATERING-POT , s. sekapAtraM, secanapAtraM, secanaGawaH, kalasaH.
WATERMAN: I Boat-man: nAvikaH.II Water-carrier: q. v.
WATERPROOF: jalABedya (f. dyA) and sim. comp. s.
WATERPROOF , a. jalABedyaH -dyA -dyaM, jalAvyApyaH &c., udakABedyaH &c.
WATERSPOUT: (1) udavajraH (?);(2) jalastamBaH (?, Akshoy).
WATERWHEEL: GawIyantram (?).
WATERWORKS: perh. jalakarman (n.) or jalIya- karman and sim. comp.s.
WATERY: (1) by comp.;(2) jalamaya (f. yI) and sim. comp. s. (= consisting of, abound- -ing in, water);(3) jalIya (f. yA) etc. (= of w.).

WATERY , a. (Pertaining to water) jalasambanDI &c., OdakaH -kI -kaM, ApyaH -pyA -pyaM, jalasaH -sA -saM, udakalaH -lA -laM. — (Con- [Page836-b+ 51] sisting of it) jalamayaH -yI -yaM, jalarUpaH -pA -paM, ammayaH &c. — (Abounding with it) jalAQyaH -QyA -QyaM, sajalaH &c., jalaprAyaH -yA -yaM, ambumAn -matI -mat (t), bahUdakaH -kA -kaM, bahujalaH -lA -laM, sasalilaH &c., sAmBAH &c., see MARSHY; ‘watery wave,’ jalormmiH m. f.
Wattle, s. kAzWAvaraRaM. 2 praSAKA.
WATTLE: I Hurdle: kAzWabanDaH.II Of cocks: Pullam.
WATTLE , s. kAzWaSalAkAgraTitam avaroDakaM, kAzWaSalAkAgraTitastamBaH.
To WATTLE , v. a. kAzWaSalAkAH parasparaM granT. See To INTERWEAVE.

Wave, s. taraMgaH, Urmi f., vIci-cI f., kallolaH, BaMgaH, BaMgi-gI f. v. t. DU 5, 9 U or c. (DUnayati), vi-A-°, cal c., saM-, Ir c. 2 utsfj 6 P, parityaj 1 P. v. i. itastataH pra-vi-cal 1 P, DU pass. [Wav]y, a. taraMgita, Urmimat, kallolamaya (yI f.), BaMgimat, BaMgura, unnatAnata.
WAVE (subs.): (1) taraNgaH, large w. s.: vfhatastara- NgAn, R.;(2) UrmiH, w. crowned: UrmimAlin (f. nI);(3) BaNgiH: v. Also billow.
WAVE (v. t.): (1) DUnayati (DU, c. 10. = shake: q. v.);(2) cAlayati (c. of cal = move: q. v.).
WAVE (v. i.): (1) DUyate (pass. of Du.): v. Shake;(2) calati (cal, c. 1.): v. To move.

WAVE , s. UrmmiH m. f., UrmmikA, jalormmiH f., taraNgaH, jalataraNgaH, vIciH m. f., BaNgaH, BaNgiH -NgI f., BaRqiH f., kallolaH, ullolaH, jala- latA, payorASiH f.; ‘wave-crowned,’ UrmmimAlI -linI -li (n), calormmimAlI &c.

To WAVE , v. a. (Move this way and that way) itastataH saMcal in caus. (-cAlayati -yituM) or cal or AsPal in caus., Bram (c. 10. Bramayati -yituM), itastato viDU. — (Put aside, give up) tyaj (c. 1. tyajati, tyaktuM), visfj (c. 6. -sfjati -srazwuM), hA, vihA.
To WAVE , v. n. itastataS cal (c. 1. calati -lituM) or vical.
WAVELESS , a. avIciH -ciH -ci, nistaraNgaH -NgA -NgaM. See UNRUFFLED.

Waver, v. i. dolAyate (D.), dvEDIBU 1 P, saM-SI 2 A, vikxp 1 A; ‘his mind w(aver)ed being at a loss which course to follow’ ityekapakzASrayaviklavatvAdAsItsa dolAcalacittavfttiH (R. xiv. 34); oft. by anavasTita, akftaniScaya also. [Waver]ing, a. aniScita, dolAyamAna, saMdigDa, anavasTita.
WAVER: dolAyate (nomi.), with w. ing mind: dolAyamAnacetasA; w. ing: akftaniScaya (f. yA = un- -settled, unsteady: q. v.): v. Also to reel.
To WAVER , v. n. dola (nom. dolAyate), vical (c. 1. -calati -lituM).

WAVY: (1) taraNgita (f. tA), w. bank: taraNgitaM sEkatam, Ki. iv. 6.; making the banners w.: taraNgitAlambitaketusantatiH, Ki. xiv. 28.;(2) Urmi- mat (f. tI);(3) UrmimAlin (f. nI);(4) BaNgimat (f. tI), M. n.; etc.
WAVY , a. UrmmimAn -matI -mat (t), BaNguraH -rA -raM, banDuraH &c., tara- NgitaH -tA -taM, unnatAnataH &c., calaH -lA -laM. See UNDULATING.

Wax, s. lAkzA (for sealing). 2 si(Si)kTaM, sikTakaM, maDUcCizwaM, maDujaM. 3 karRamalaM; tokmaM. v. i. vfD 1 A; ‘w(ax)ing and waning’, vfdDikzayO, ‘the moon w(ax)ed’ kalAvfdDo baBUva; ‘w(ax)ing hot’ kroDedDo BUtvA. 2 sikTakena lip 6 P or aMj 7 P. [Wax]en, [Wax]y, a. sikTamaya (yI f.), SikTAkta.
WAX (subs.): I Of bees:(1) sikTam;(2) maDUcCizwam.II For sealing: lAkzA.III Of the ear:(1) toknam;(2) karRamalam.
WAX (v.): I Intrans.: varDate (vfD, c. 1.): v. To increase.II Trans.: limpati (lip, c. 6.): v. To besmear.
WAX , s. (Of bees) sikTaM -kTakaM, maDUcCizwaM, maDujaM, SikTaM, ucCizwamodanaM, drAvakaM, kAcaM. — (For sealing) lAkzA, alaktaH. — (Of the ear) karRamalaM.
To WAX , v. a. sikTakena lip or aYj, sikTakAktaM -ktAM kf.
To WAX , v. n. (Increase) vfD; ‘as the moon,’ kalAvfdDo BU.
WAXEN, WAXY: (1) sikTamayaH (yI, yaM = made of wax);(2) sikTAkta (f. ktA = coated with wax.);(3) sikTAma (f. BA = like w.).
WAXEN , WAXY, a. sikTakamayaH -yI -yaM, sEkTikaH &c., sikTasaguRaH &c.

Way, s. mArgaH, paTin m., aDvan m., vartman n., padavi-vI f., ayanaM, saraRi-RI f., padDati-tI f., padyA; ‘step in a wrong w(ay)’ apaTe padamarpayaMti (R. ix. 74). 2 aMtaraM, mAtraM, paryaMtaH; ‘a little w(ay)’ IzaddUraM, stokAMtaraM. 3 upAyaH, yukti f. 4 prakAraH, viDiH, rIti f., kramaH, mArgaH; ‘a good way’ atipaMTAH, supaMTAH, satpaTaH, supaTaH; ‘a bad or wrong w(ay)’ apaMTAH; apaTaH, vyaDvaH, duraDvaH, vimArgaH, vipaTaH, kadaDvan m., kA(ku)paTaH; ‘a place where four w(ay)s meet’ SfMgAwakaH, catuzpaTaM; ‘a dreary w(ay)’ prAMtaraM, dUraSUnyoDvA ‘difficult w(ay)’ kAMtAraH-raM, durgamaM vartma, durgasaMcaraH, saMkramaH. 5 (With numerals) Ex. by DA; ‘in two w(ay)s’ dviDA; SataDA &c.; ‘a long w(ay) off’ sudUraM, ‘on the w(ay)’ aMtarA, aMtare, ‘stand or come in the (oneʼs) w(ay)’ paripaMTIBU, aMtarAyaH &c. (‘Obstacle’, q. v.) BU; (lit.) nayanapaTaM-vizayaM-yA 2 P; ‘in this, that-w(ay)’ itTaM-evaM, taTA; ‘by w(ay) of example’ nidarSanadvArA-rUpeRa; ‘lead the w(ay)’ mArgaM AdiS 6 P or dfS c.; ‘this w(ay)’, ‘this w(ay)’ ita ita; ‘by w(ay) of’ dvAreRa, rUpeRa; ‘make w(ay)’ apasara, apehi aMtaraM dIyatAM; ‘in every way’ sarvaTA; ‘in another w(ay)’ anyaTA, ‘w(ay)-farer’ paTikaH; See Traveller; ‘w(ay)-lay’ paTi niBftaM pratIkz 1 A (luMWanArTaM, vaDArTaM), paTi avaskaMd 1 P; ‘w(ay)-ward’ pratIpa, svErin, durlalita; See Obstinate; ‘w(ay)-worn’ aDvaSrAMta, aDvasaMjAtaKeda.

WAY: I Road:(1) mArgaH, to give w.: mArgaM dadAti, Mr. x.; to lead the w.: mArgamAdiSati, Sa. v.;(2) panTAH, tell me the w. which leads to the hermitage of Agastya: agastyASramasya panTAnaM brUhi, U. ii.; tread in improper w. s.: apaTe padamarpayanti, R. ix. 74.;(3) aDvan (m.), going a little w.: gatvA kaYcidaDvAnam, K.; accidentally in the w.: aDvani dEvayogAt, R. v. 60.;(4) vartman (n.), one who has lost his w.: pranazwavartman (mfn.), K.; women go the w. of their husbands: pramadAH pati- [Page756] vartmagAH, Ku. iv. 33. Ph.: I have come such a long w.: etAvatIM BUmiBAyAtaH, K.; this w. your majesty: ito ito devI, V. ii.; did you not see (meet) the Queen on the w.: na Kalvantare tvayA dfzwA devI, Sa. vi.; make w.: antaramantaram, Mr. x.; which w. is the wretch gone: katamena digvi- BAgena gataH sa jAlmaH ? V. i.; right of w.: gamanADi- kAraH.II Device: q. v.: upAyaH.III Manner, method: q. v.: prakAraH. Miscell.: in two, three, many w. s: dviDA, triDA, bahuDA; by w. of illustration: nidarSanarUpeRa.

WAY , s. (Road, path) mArgaH, paTaH, panTAH m. (paTin), aDvA m. (n), vartma n. (n), ayanaM, see ROAD; ‘one who has lost his way,’ mArgaBrazwaH, vartmavarjitaH, digBrAntaH; ‘to give way,’ mArgaM dA, panTAnaM tyaj; ‘make way! make way!’ apasara, apasarata, avasara, antaram antaraM. — (Space, distance) antaraM, mAtraM, paryyantaM, dUraM; ‘for a little way,’ kiyatparyyantaM, kiyaddUraM, IzaddUraM; ‘a great way,’ ati- dUraM. — (Direction) dik f. (S), mArgaH; ‘to point out the way,’ dikpradarSanaM kf, mArgaM dfS in caus., mArgapradarSanaM kf; ‘this way, this way!’ ita itas; ‘which way?’ kutra, kAM diSaM; ‘in both ways,’ uBayatra. — (Manner, method, course) prakAraH, rItiH f., viDiH m., viDAnaM, kramaH, mArgaH; ‘way to act,’ kriyAviDiH m., kftyaviDiH m., see MANNER. Often expressed by the affix DA; as, ‘in one way,’ ekaDA; ‘in two ways,’ dviDA; ‘in three,’ triDA; ‘in a hundred,’ SataDA; ‘in many,’ bahuDA, ane- kaDA; ‘in how many?’ katiDA; ‘that may be written in two ways,’ dviDAleKyaH -KyA -KyaM. Or by the affixes TA, tas, &c.; as, ‘in both ways,’ uBayaTA, uBayatas.
WAY-WORN , a. aDvaSrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, mArgaSrAntaH &c., yAnaSrAntaH &c.
WAYFARER: (1) paTikaH;(2) aDvanInaH;(3) aDvanyaH;(4) aDvagaH.
WAYFARER , s. paTikaH, aDvagaH, mArgikaH, aDvanyaH. See TRAVELLER.
WAYLAY: paTi avaskandate (skand, c. 1. = attack: q. v.). or niBftaM pratIkzate (Ikz, c. 1. = wait: q. v.).
To WAYLAY , v. a. parAkramaRArTaM mArge niBftaM sTA.
WAYSIDE: expr. by comp., w. trees: mArgaSAKinaH R. i. 45.: v. Border.
WAYWARD: pratIpa (f. pA): v. Perverse, wil- -ful, forward.
WAYWORN: (1) aDvaSrAnta (f. ntA);(2) aDvanA pariklAnta (f. ntA), Ki. xi. 2.; and sim. comp. s.
WE: vayam. Ph.: here are we: ime smaH, Sa. iv.
WE , pron. vayaM nom. pl. (asmad); ‘we two,’ AvAM nom. du.

Weak, a. durbala, aSakta, abala, kzIRabala, bala-Sakti-hIna, niHsattva, nistejas, nirvIrya, alpa-bala-Sakti. 2 (In mind) maMda, alpaDI, vikalacitta; ‘w(eak) point or side’ CidraM, raMDraM, dozaH, marmasTAnaM. [Weak]en, v. t. durbalIkf 8 U, SaktiM-balaM hf 1 P, SaktiM ava-sad c. or apaci 5 U; ‘to be w(eaken)ed’ apaci pass.; See Waste, Lean. [Weaken]ed, a. hftabala, kzIRaSakti, hrasva (form). [Weak]ness, s. dOrbalyaM, bala or Sakti-kzayaH or nASaH, asAmarTyaM, bala-sattva-hAni f. 2 dozaH, (yOvana--dozAH); CidraM.

WEAK: (1) durbala (f. lA), the strong would have roasted the w.: apakzyan durbalAn balavattarAH, M. vii. 20.; w. digestion: durbalo'gniH, Bha.;(2) abala (f. lA), eating their own w. brothers: abalasva- kulASinaH, N. ii. 10.;(3) balahIna (f. nA), S.;(4) kzIRabala (f. lA), Bha.; and sim. comp. s: v. Also feeble, slender, decay. Ph.: w. point: dozaH (fault: q. v.), Cidram (= hole: q. v.).

WEAK , a. durbalaH -lA -laM, nirbalaH &c., abalaH &c., alpabalaH &c., alpa- SaktiH -ktiH -kti, akalpaH -lpA -lpaM, niHsattvaH -ttvA -ttvaM, nistejAH -jAH -jaH (s), see FEEBLE, INFIRM. — (In mind) alpabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, alpaDIH -DIH -Di, vikalabudDiH &c., vikalAntaHkaraRaH -RA -RaM. — [Page837-a+ 51] (Weak point or side) CidraM, marmmasTAnaM.
WEAKEN: (1) durbalIkaroti;(2) balakzayaM karoti (with gen.);(3) balaM harati (hf, c. 1. = remove: q. v.) or kziRoti (kzi, c. 5. = waste: q. v.).
To WEAKEN , v. a. durbalIkf, balaM hf (c. 1. harati, harttuM), balakzayaM kf, SaktikzayaM kf, SaktiBaNgaM kf, SaktihrAsaM kf. See To DEBILITATE.
WEAKENED , p. p. kzIRabalaH -lA -laM, hftabalaH &c., durbalIkftaH -tA -taM, hftOjAH -jAH -jaH (s), kzIRasattvaH -ttvA -ttvaM. See ENFEEBLED.
WEAKENING , a. balakzayakArI -riRI -ri (n), sattvakzayakArI &c.
WEAKLY: I Adj.: kzIRabala (f. lA): v. Weak. II Adv.:(1) durbalam;(2) by adj. or cir- -cumlo.: v. Also in vain.

WEAKNESS: I In gen.:(1) durbalatA, -tvam or dOrbalyam, w. of a king: dOrbalyaM rAjYaH, M. viii. 171.; w. of the senses: indriyARAM dOrbalyam, Bha.;(2) abala (rare), strength and w. of the enemy: amitrabalAbalam, M. n. on Si. ii. 36.; (3) balahInatA and sim. deriv. s.II Foible, fault: q. v.: vyasanam.
WEAKNESS , s. durbalatA, dOrbalyaM, nirbalatA, abalaM, aSaktiH f., balahInatA, balakzayaH, SaktikzayaH, balakzIRatA, balahAniH f., SaktiBaNgaH, see DE- BILITY. — (Foible) CidraM.
Weal, s. hitaM, kalyARaM, kzemaM, Sreyas n., BadraM, kuSalaM; ‘w(eal) and woe’ SuBASuBaM.
WEAL: I Welfare, happiness: q. v.: kzemam. Ph.: for the public w.: prakftihitAya, Sa. vii. II Mark of a blow: kzatacihnam.
WEAL , s. kzemaM, kalyARaM, SuBaM, Sreyas, BadraM, kuSalaM, see WELFARE; ‘weal and woe,’ SuBASuBaM, BadrABadraM.

sanskrit.slp1: Danena kiM yo na dadAti nASnute
sanskrit.word: धनेन किं यो न ददाति नाश्नुते
sanskrit.iast: dhanena kiṃ yo na dadāti nāśnute

details.body: Wealth, s. DanaM, dravyaM, vasuH n. arTaH, vittaM, draviRaM, saMpad f., hiraRyaM, viBavaH, vEBavaM, saMpatti f., ESvaryaM, rE f., ri(f)kTaM, dyumnaM, svApateyaM; ‘w(ealth) in cattle’ goDanaM. [Wealth]y, a. Danin, Danika, Dana-vitta-vat &c., saDana, vittasaMpanna, saSrIka, vasumat, arTayukta, viBavaSAlin and sim. comp.

WEALTH: I Riches:(1) Danam (= pro. money), what is the use of w. (to one) who does not give, does not eat: Danena kiM yo na dadAti nASnute, H.; (2) vasu (n. = 1), not only the w. of the monarch: vasu tasya vimorna kevalam, R.;(3) viBavaH;(4) vEBavam;(5) ESvaryam;(6) sampattiH (= property); (7) vittam (= 1).II Prosperity: q. v.

WEALTH , s. DanaM, vasu n., vittaM, viBavaH, vEBavaM, sampattiH f., draviRaM, dravyaM, rAH m. (rE), rikTaM, fkTaM, hiraRyaM, dyumnaM, svApateyaM, BogyaM, see RICHES; ‘in grain,’ DAnyaDanaM, DAnyArTaH; ‘in cattle,’ goDanaM, carmmaDanaM.
WEALTHINESS , s. mahADanatA, saDanatvaM. See RICHNESS, OPULENCE.
WEALTHY: mahADana (f. nA): v. Rich.
WEALTHY , a. DanI -ninI -ni (n). See RICH, OPULENT.
Wean, v. t. stanyaM tyaj c. or hA c. (hApayati) or visfj c. 2 viraktI-vimuKI-kf 8 U; See Separate. [Wean]ing, s. stanyatyAgaH. 2 virakti f., vErAgyaM, saMgatyAgaH.
WEAN: I Lit.: stanyaM tyAjayati, pari- (c. of tyaj) or hApayati, pari- (c. of hA) or visarjayati (c. of sfj).II Fig.: viyojayati (yuj, c. 10) or viDawayati (Gaw, c. 10.): v. To separate.

To WEAN , v. a. tyaktastanyaM -nyAM kf, stanyaviyuktaM -ktAM kf, stanyaM -tyaj in caus. (tyAjayati -yituM), stanyatyAgaM kf. — (From the world) saNga- vimuKaM -KAM kf, vizayavimuKaM -KAM kf, tyaktasaNgaM -NgAM kf, viraktaM -ktAM kf.
WEANED , p. p. tyaktastanyaH -nyA -nyaM, tyaktastanaH -nA -naM. See To WEAN.
WEANING , WEANEDNESS, s. stanyatyAgaH; ‘from the world,’ saNgatyAgaH, vErAgyaM, vizayAsaNgaH, indriyAsaNgaH, vizayavimuKatA, pratyAhAraH.
Weapon, s. SastraM, astraM, AyuDaM, praharaRaM, heti f.

WEAPON: (1) Sastram, when victory was not inter- cepted by w. s.: SastrEravyaDIyamAnavijayaH, Vi. v. 51.; (2) astram (properly a missile), various w.: viviDamastram, Ki. xviii. 46.;(3) AyuDam;(4) praharaRam;(5) hetiH (rare).
WEAPON , s. SastraM, AyuDaM, astraM, praharaRaM, hetiH f., pariGAtaH, baDatraM, SastrAstraM.

Wear, v. t. pari-DA 3 U, Df 1 P, 10, Bf 3 U, vas 2 A. 2 (Away) kzi 5 P, naS c., vilup c., pramfj 2 P or c.; GarzaRena naS c. 3 jIrRIkf 8 U. 4 ava-, sad c. Kid c., klam c.; glE c.; See Fatigue. v. i. (Away) kzi pass., avasad 1 P, apaci pass. 2 (By use) jF 4 P, jarjarIBU 1 P; ‘when the night had almost worn away’ kzIRaBUyizWAyAM kzapAyAM; ‘w(ear) off’ apagam 1 P, naS 4 P, kzi pass.; ‘w(ear) out’ jIrRI-jarjarI-kf, apaci; (v. i.) jF, jyA 9 P, jarjarIBU. s. pari-, kzayaH, apacayaH upayogaH. 2 GarzaRaM. 3 setuH, Ali f. [Wear]er, s. DArin, Bft in comp. [Wear]ing, a. DArin, Bft, Dara in comp. 2 pariDAnayogya.
WEAR (subs.): I Waste: q. v.: kzayaH, pari-, ava-.II Dress: q. v.: vAsas (n.).III Dam: banDaH.

WEAR (v. t.): I To put on: q. v.: Darati or DArayati (Df, c. 1. and 10), ornaments worn by women during the life-time of their husbands: patyO jIvati yaH strIBiralaNkAro Dfto Bavet, Mit.; clothes etc., worn by a father.: pitfDftaM vastrAdikam, Mit. Ph.: w. ing apparel: pariDAnavAsas, (n.) and sim. comp. s.II To impair: kziRoti (kzi, c. 5.): v. Waste.
WEAR (v. t.): kzIyate (pass. of kzi): v. To waste.

To WEAR , v. a. (Impair, consume by attrition, &c.) kzi in caus. (kzapayati, kzayayati -yituM), kzayaM kf, Gfz (c. 1. Garzati -rzituM), GarzaRena naS. — (Carry on the body, as clothes, &c.) Df (c. 10. DAra- yati -yituM, c. 1. Darati, DarttuM), Bf (c. 3. biBartti, c. 1. Barati, BarttuM), DA (c. 3. Datte, DAtuM), pariDA, ACad (c. 10. -CAdayati -yituM), vas (c. 2. vaste -situM); ‘he wears clothes,’ vAsAMsi biBartti. — (Wear out by use, &c.) jIrRaM -rRAM kf, jIrRIkf, jarjjarIkf, jarjjaraM -rAM kf. — (Wear out, consume by fatigue, &c.) sad (c. 10. sAdayati -yituM), avasad, Kid (c. 10. Kedayati -yituM), glE in caus. (glapayati -yituM), see To FATIGUE.

To WEAR , v. n. (Waste away) kzi in pass. (kzIyate), sad, see To WASTE, v. n. — (Wear out by use) jF (c. 4. jIryyati), parijF, jIrRaH -rRA -rRaM BU, jIrRIBU, jarjjaraH -rA -raM BU, jarjjarIBU. — (Wear off), see To PASS AWAY.
WEAR , s. (Waste through use) kzayaH, parikzayaH, avakzayaH, upaBogaH, BogaH. — (Friction) GarzaRaM, AGarzaRaM. — (Dam in a river) setuH m., jalapravAhabanDaH.
WEAR OFF: (1) naSyati (naS, c. 4.): v. Des- -troy;(2) apagacCati (gam, c. 1.): v. To go away.
WEAR OUT: I By use:(1) jIrRIkaroti;(2) jarjarIkaroti.II Intrans.: jIryati, pari- (jF, c. 4.);(2) jIrRIBavati;(3) jarjarIBavati.III To fatigue, tire: q. v.: sAdayati, ava- (c. of sad).
WEARER , s. DArI m. (n), DaraH, vasitA m. (tf), Bft m.
WEARIED: (1) klAnta (f. ntA);(2) pariSrAnta (f. ntA): v. Fatigued.
WEARIED , p. p. SrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, klAntaH &c. See FATIGUED.
WEARINESS: (1) klamaH;(2) klAntiH: Fatigue.
WEARINESS , s. SramaH, SrAntiH f., klAntiH f., KedaH. See FATIGUE.
WEARING , part. or a. (Carrying) DArI -riRI -ri (n), DaraH -rA -raM, udvahan -hantI &c. — (Consuming) kzayakArI &c. — (Fit to wear) pariDAnopayogI -ginI &c., pariDAnayogyaH -gyA -gyaM.
WEARISOME: (1) Sramajanana (f. nI);(2) AyAsa- kara (f. rI);(3) svedajanaka (f. nikA); etc.

WEARISOME , a. SramajanakaH -kA -kaM, KedajanakaH &c., AyAsajanakaH &c., SrAntikaraH -rI -raM, SramakaraH &c., SramakArakaH -kA -kaM, AyAsajanakaH &c., kazwajanakaH &c., kazwapradaH -dA -daM. See TEDIOUS.

Weary, v. t. Ayas c., klam c., Kid c. v. i. Ayas 1, 4 P, klam 1, 4 P. [Wear]ied, a. Kinna, klAMta, pariSrAMta, mlAna, jAtaKeda; ‘w(earied) of’ nirviRRa, nirvedemApanna; See Disgusted; ‘w(earied) of life’ jIvitAdudvijamAnaH (Mal. 3). [Wear]iness, s. klamaH, SramaH, KedaH, AyAsaH; See Fatigue, [Fatigu]ed &c. [Wear]isome, a. Srama-Keda-janana (nI f.), AyAsakara (rI f.), SramAvaha, kazwaprada.
WEARY (adj.): I Fatigued: q. v.: klAnta (f. ntA).II Wearisome.
WEARY (v.): AyAsayati (c. of yas): v. To fatigue.
To WEARY , v. a. Ayas (c. 10. -yAsayati -yituM). See To FATIGUE.
To WEARY , v. n. Kid (c. 4. Kidyate), Sram (c. 4. SrAmyati), Ayas (c. 4. -yasyati).
WEARY , a. SrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, klAntaH &c., KinnaH -nnA -nnaM, glAnaH -nA -naM, mlAnaH &c., tandrAluH -lA -lu, jAtaKedaH -dA -daM. See FATIGUED.
Weasel, s. nakulaH, baBruH, aMgUzaH.
WEASEL: (1) nakulaH;(2) baBruH (rare).
WEASEL , s. nakulaH, aNgUzaH, baBruH m., sUcivadanaH.

Weather, s. kAlaH, dinaM; ‘bad w(eather)’ durdinaM; ‘good w(eather)’ sudinaM; ‘if the w(eather) be fine’ yadi durdinaM na syAt; ‘w(eather)-beaten’ vAtAhata, praBaMjanopahata; ‘weather-glass’, s. vAyumApakayaMtraM; ‘w(eather)-wise’ vAtAdilakzaRavid, kAlavid. v. t. tF 1 P, pratyavasTA 1 A; pAraM gam 1 P.
WEATHER (v.): I To air: q. v.:II To sail to the windward of: prativAtamatikrAmati (kram, c. 1.): v. To cross.III Fig.: tarati (ta, c. 1.): v. To cross, bear, sustain.
WEATHER (subs.): (1) by circumlo.;(2) kAlaH (= time: q. v.);(3) dinam. Ph.: bad w.: durdinam, vArdalam; good w.: sudinam.
WEATHER , s. kAlaH, samayaH, dinaM; ‘fine weather,’ sudinaM, sudinAhaH -haM, uttamAhaH; ‘bad weather,’ durdinaM, vArdalaM.
To WEATHER , v. a. duHKena pAr (c. 10. pArayati -yituM) or tIr (c. 10. tIrayati -yituM), kazwena tIraM or pAraM gam, duHKena tF.
WEATHER-BEATEN: (1) vAtAhata (f. tA: by wind);(2) BaYBAhata (f. tA: by hurricane); etc.
WEATHER-BEATEN , a. vAtAhataH -tA -taM, vAtavfzwyAhataH tA -taM, aBrAvakA- SikaH -kA -kaM.
WEATHER-COCK , s. prAsAdaSfNgAgre sTApitaM kukkuwAkAraM vAyulakzaRaM.
WEATHER-GLASS: vAyuyantram.
WEATHER-GLASS . s. vAyumApakayantraM, vAyugurutvajYApakayantraM.
WEATHER-PROOF , a. vAtavfzwyaBedyaH -dyA -dyaM, vfzwyaBedyaH &c.
WEATHER-WISE: vAtAdilakzaRavida (mfn.) and sim. comp.s.
WEATHER-WISE , a. kAladarSanakuSalaH -lA -laM, kAlavid m. f. n.
WEATHERCOCK: vAyupradarSinI and sim. comp. s.
Weave, v. t. ve 1 P; vap 1 P, guM(gu)P 6 P, vi-, rac 10. [Weav]er, s. taMtuvAyaH-paH, kuviMdaH, pawakAraH. [Weav]ing, s. vAyaH-paH, taMtu-taMtra-vAyaH, Uti-vyUti. f. pawanirmARaM, pawakarman n.
WEAVE: vyati, pra- (ve, c. 1.), w. ing cloth: pawaM vayantO, Mah. i. 3. 140.
To WEAVE , v. a. ve (c. 1. vayati, vAtuM), vap (c. 1. vapati -ptuM), Uy (c. 1. Uyate -yituM), gumP (c. 6. gumPati -mPituM), guP, rac (c. 10. racayati -yituM), virac.
To WEAVE , v. n. (Practise weaving) vAyaM kf, tantuvAya kf, vApaM kf, tantuvApaM kf, sUtravApaM kf, tantuvyUtiM kf, sUtravezwanaM kf.
WEAVER: (1) tantu(ntra)vAyaH(paH);(2) kuvi(pi)ndaH; (3) pawwakAraH, -kaH.
WEAVER , s. tantuvAyaH, tantuvApaH, tantravAyaH, tantravApaH, tandravAyaH, kuvindaH, kupindaH, pawakAraH, sUcISilpopajIvI m. (n).

WEAVING , s. vAyaH, vApaH, tantuvAyaH, tantuvApaH, sUtravAyaH, UtiH f., vyUtiH f., vyutiH f., tAntavaM, vARiH f., veRiH f., sUtravezwanaM, pawanirmmARaM, viracanA, trasaraH; ‘Room for weaving,’ tantuSAlA.
Web, s. jAlaM, taMtra-taMtu-saMtati f.; (of the eye) pawalaM; ‘w(eb)-footed’ jAlapAda.
WEB: I gen.: jAlam.II Of the eye: pawalam.
WEB , s. tantusantataM -tiH f., sUtrasantatiH f., tantraM, jAlaM. — (Of the eye) pawalaM. — (Of a spider) UrRanABajAlaH, see SPIDER.
WEB-FOOTED: jAlapAdaH (f. dA); a w. animal: kaScijjAlapAdaH, D. i.
WEB-FOOTED , a. jAlapAdaH -dA -daM, jAlapAd, jAlAkArapAdaH &c.

Wed, v. t. vi-ud-vah 1 P, pari-RI 1 P. [Wed]ded, a. UQa, pariRIta. 2 Asakta, avalaMbin, rakzin, (to an opinion); ‘w(ed)lock’ vivAhaH; ‘a wife married in w(ed)lock’ DarmapatnI, sahaDarmacAriRI; See Marriage.
WED: pariRayati (nI, c. 1.): v. To marry.
To WED , v. a. vivah, pariRI, pARigrahaRaM kf. See To MARRY.
WEDDED: Fig.: Asakta (f. ktA): v. Atta- -ched.

WEDDED , p. p. or a. vivAhitaH -tA -taM, pariRItaH &c., kftakaragrahaH -hA -haM, see MARRIED; ‘wedded woman,’ UQA; ‘wedded couple,’ dampatI m. du. — (Strongly attached) AsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, rataH -tA -taM; ‘to one's own opinion,’ svamatarakzI -kziRI &c.
WEDDING: vivAhaH: v. Marriage.
WEDDING , s. vivAhotsavaH, vivAhaparvva n. (n), vivAhaH, udvAhakarmma n. (n), vivAhasaMskAraH, vivAhakriyA; ‘wedding dress,’ vivAhanepaTyaM, vEvAhikanepaTyaM.
Wedge, s. kIlaH, SaMkuH. v. t. saMpIq 10, saMbAD 1 A, saMmfd 9 P.
WEDGE , s. kIlaH, kIlakaH, SaNkuH m.
To WEDGE , v. a. saMhan, sampIq, sambAD, bAD, sammfd.
WEDLOCK: vivAhaH: v. Marriage.
WEDLOCK , s. vivAhasambanDaH, vivAhitAvasTA, dArakarmma n. (n).
Wednesday, s. buDavAsaraH.
WEDNESDAY: (1) buDavAraH;(2) buDavAsaraH;(3) sOmyavAraH.
WEDNESDAY , s. buDavAraH, sOmyavAraH -vAsaraH, kulAkulavAraH.

Weed, s. kakzaH, tfRAdikaM, staMbaH; (fig.) gatiroDanaM, prasarastaMBanaM. 2 (‘W(eed)s’) vAsas n.; See Garment; ‘widowʼs w(eed)s’ klizwanivasanaM, cIraM. v. t. (Out) (kakzaM) ud-hf 1 P, nirdo 4 P, utpaw 10. [Weed]er, s. nirdAtf m., kakzodDArin m. [Weed]y, a. kakzapUrRa-bahula.

WEED (subs.): I A noxious plant:(1) kakzaH, to take up w. s: kakzamudDarati, M. vii. 110.;(2) tfRAdikam, R. t.;(3) perh. agacCaH. (comp. Bengalee AgACA).II Widow's dress: perh. klizwanibasanam, D. v.; cIram or cIvaram (prop. rag).
WEED (v.): udDarati (Df, c. 1.); (2) nirdAti or -dyati (dA, c. 2. or do, c. 4.).
WEED , s. kakzaH, stambaH, tfRaM, kaRwakaH -kaM; ‘instrument for de- stroying weeds,’ stambaGnaH. — (Widow's weeds) cIraM, cIvaraM.
To WEED , v. a. kakzam udDf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM), tfRAni utpaw (c. 10. -pAwayati -yituM) or ucCid, vitfRIkf.
WEEDER: (1) nirdAtf (f. trI), M. vii. 110.; (2) kakzodDartf (f. rtrI) and sim. comp. s.
WEEDING , s. kakzodDaraRaM, kakzocCedaH, tfRodDaraRaM, kaRwakodDaraRaM.
WEEDY , a. kakzapUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, kakzabahulaH -lA -laM, tfRapUrRaH &c.
Week, s. saptAhaH, saptadinaM; ‘w(eek)day’ vAraH. [Week]ly, a. sAptAhika (kI f.), saptadEnika (kI f.). adv. pratisaptAhaM.
WEEK: saptAham, every w.: saptahAt saptAhAt, Sr; w. day: vAraH.
WEEK , s. saptAhaM, vArasaptakaM, dinasaptakaM; ‘week-day,’ vAraH.
WEEKLY: I Adj.: sAptAhika (f. kI).II Adv.: saptAhe saptAhe.
WEEKLY , a. sAptAhikaH -kI -kaM, saptAhnikaH &c., saptadEnikaH &c.
WEEKLY , adv. saptAhe saptAhe, pratisaptAhaM.
Ween, v. i. man 4 A; See Think; ‘over w(een)ing’ atyaMtABimAnin.
WEEN: manyate (man, c. 4.): v. To think.
Weep, v. i. rud 2 P, vi-lap 1 P, aSrURi pat c. or vimuc 6 P, A-, kraMd 1 P; See Cry, Lament. [Weep]ing, s. ruditaM, rodanaM, vilApaH, AkraMdanaM, kraMditaM, aSrupAtaH. a. sAsru, aSrulocana.

WEEP: (1) roditi, pra-, aBi- (rud, c. 2.), how will you get (her) w. ing: rudatA kuta eva laByate, R. viii. 85.; embracing (me) w.ing: saruditaM parizvajya, D. iii.;(2) vilapati (lap, c. 1. = bewail); (3) aSrURi pAtayati (= shed tears): v. Also to cry.
To WEEP , v. n. rud (c. 10. roditi -tuM), krand (c. 1. krandati -ndituM), aSrURi pat in caus., see To CRY; ‘weep not,’ mA'rOtsIH.
WEEPING (subs.): (1) rodanam;(2) ruditam;(3) krandanam;(4) kranditam;(5) vilApaH (= lamen- -tation).
WEEPING , s. krandanaM, rodanaM, aSrupAtaH. See LAMENTATION.
WEEPING , part. rudan -datI &c., aSrulocanaH -nI -naM, upaplutAkzaH &c.
WEEPING-WILLOW: vfkzaviSezaH; namraSAKaH.
WEEVIL: kIwaviSezaH, *jAlakIwaH.

Weigh, v. t. tul-tUl 10, tulAyAM Df 10. 2 (In mind) vi-mfS 6 P, Aloc 10, vi-car c., vi-gaR 10; See Think. 3 (Anchor) uttul; ‘w(eigh) down’ aBi-BU 1 P, AkulIkf; ‘w(eigh) duly’ paricCid 7 P, sUkzmaM nirUp 10. v. t. Ex. by ‘Weight’ q. v.; ‘what does it w(eigh)’ kiMBAramidaM kiM BAraparimARaM; ‘w(eigh) upon’ pIq 10, bAD 1 A; See Afflict; ‘w(eigh) with’ man pass.; ‘dress w(eigh)s much with them’ vezastErbahu manyate. [Weigh]ing, s. tolanaM, vigaRanA-naM. Weight, s. mAnaM, BAraH, tolaH, parimARaM, BAraparimARaM, gurutvaM, 2 gurutvaM, gOravaM, praBAvaH, BAraH. 3 BAraH, Dur f.; ‘of little w(eight)’ laGvarTa, laGupraBAva, aguru. [Weight]y, a. guru, mahat, sapraBAva, sapramARa.

WEIGH (v. t.): I Lit.:(1) tolayati or tUlayati (tul or tUl, c. 10.), if increases when w. ed: tulito yadi varDate, N. s.;(2) tulAyAM karoti or DArayati (prop. in a balance), if truth is w. ed with thousand horse-sacrifices: aSvameDasahasrARi satyaYca tulayA Dftam, H. iv. 131.II As anchor: tolayati, ut-: v. To lift, raise.III To ponder, consider: q. v.: vimfSati (mfS, c. 6.) Comp., w. down: v. To overcome, oppress.
WEIGH (v. i.): expr. by subs. or adj., The dove w. ed greater: gurutara eva kapota AsIt, Mah. iii. 197. 21.; what does it w.: kiMBAraBidam. Comp. w. upon: pIqayati (pIq, c. 10.): v. To press, pain.

To WEIGH , v. a. (In a balance) tul (c. 10. tulayati -yituM), tUl (c. 10. tUlayati -yituM), tolanaM kf, tulanAM kf. — (Raise, as an anchor, &c.) uttul. — (Ponder) vigaR (c. 10. -gaRayati -yituM), manasA vicar, see To PONDER; ‘to weigh alternatives,’ vikxp (c. 10. -kalpayati -yituM). ‘Weighs upon,’ viqambayati; ‘weighs down,’ see To OUTWEIGH.

To WEIGH , v. n. (Have weight) BArI -riRI -ri BU or as, BAra- vAn -vatI -vad as or BU, BArAnvitaH -tA -tam as or BU; ‘what does this weigh?’ etat kimBAram asti or etasya kiM BAraparimARaM. — (Be important) guruH -rvI -ru BU.
WEIGHED , p. p. (In a balance) tulitaH -tA -taM, tulayADftaH &c., unmitaH &c., tulAmitaH &c. — (Pondered) suvicAritaH -tA -taM.
WEIGHER , s. tolanakArI m. (n), tulADAraRavid, tulanAkft.
WEIGHING (subs.): I Lit.: tolanam.II Fig.: vigaRanam, -nA: v. Consideration.
WEIGHING , s. tolanaM, tulADAraRaM. — (Pondering) vigaRanaM -nA.

WEIGHT: I For measuring: mAnam, ut-, true and false w. s: pUrRApUrRe mAne, P.; names of w. s: mAnapariBAzA.II Heaviness, burden: q. v.: BAraH, w. of iron: lohaBAraH, P.III Impor- -tance: q. v.: gurutvam.

WEIGHT , s. (Weight or quantity ascertained by balance) BAraH, BAraparimARaM, unmAnaM, mitiH f., parimARaM, BAramitiH f., tolaH, tulA, gurutvaM -tA, gOravaM, garimA m. (n), BaraH; ‘of deficient weight,’ nyUnatolaH -lA -laM. — (Mass to weigh with) tolaM, unmAnaM. For the different weights, see under MEASURE; ‘measure by weight,’ tulAmAnaM. — (Ponderous load, burden) BAraH, DurA, DUH f. (Dur), see BURDEN. — (Importance, influence) gOravaM, gurutvaM -tA, praBAvaH, BAraH, pramARaM; ‘of little weight,’ alpapraBAvaH -vA -vaM, alpapramARaH -RA -RaM, laGupraBAvaH &c.
WEIGHTY: guru (f. also rvI): v. Heavy, im- -portant.
WEIGHTY , a. (Having weight) BArI -riRI -ri (n), guruH -rvI -ru, see HEAVY, PONDEROUS. — (Important, influential) guruH &c., sapramARaH -RA -RaM, see IMPORTANT.
Weir, s. baMDaH, yogaH.
WEIR: (1) banDaH (?);(2) yogaH (?), Mah.
WEIR , s. jalapravAhabanDakaH, jalabanDakaH, jalapratibanDakaH.
Weird, s. viDiH, aBicAra-mantraH. a. atimAnuza.

Welcome, a. svAgata. 2 SuBa, izwa, hita; priya, aBimata, suKada. v. t. svAgataM vyAhf 1 P, saBAj 10, aBinaMd 1 P, satkf 8 U, pUj 10; (ASramamfgEraBinaMditAgamanezu saBIrezu Ka. 49). interj. svAgataM (with dat.) s. svAgataM, saBAjanaM, aBinaMdanaM.
WELCOME (adj.): I Lit.: svAgata (f. tA).II Propitious, good: q. v.: SuBa (f. BA).
WELCOME (v.): (1) saBAjayati (saBAj, c. 10.): v. To greet;(2) aBinandati (nand, c. 1.): v. To cheer, salute;(3) satkaroti; pUjayati (pUj, c. 10.): v. To honour.
WELCOME (interj.): svagatam (with dat.).
WELCOME (subs.): I Lit.: svAgatam, w. to you sir: svAgatamAryAya, Mr. i.; bade him w.: tasmE svAgataM vyAjahAra, Me. i. 4.II Fig.: saBAjanam: v. Greeting, salute, honour.
WELCOME , s. svAgataM, aBinandanaM, AnandanaM, saBAjanaM, svaBAjanaM, Ama- ntraRaM, ApracCanaM; ‘word of welcome,’ svAgatavacanaM, see SALUTA- TION; ‘of a guest,’ AgatasvAgataM.
WELCOME , a. svAgataH -tA -taM. — (Grateful) suKadaH -dA -daM.

To WELCOME , v. a. svAgatam iti vad (c. 1. vadati -dituM), svAgatavacanena pUj (c. 10. pUjayati -yituM), svasti or svastivacanaM vad, Amantr (c. 10. -mantrayati -yituM), praSaMs (c. 1. -SaMsati -sitaM); ‘a new-comer,’ AgatasvAgataM kf, AgatasatkAraM kf.
WELCOMED , p. p. svAgatapUjitaH -tA -taM, satkftaH &c., samupaveSitaH &c.
WELD: saMyojayati (yuj, c. 10.): v. To unite.
To WELD , v. a. ayoGanAGAtena taptalohaM taptalohena saMyuj.
Welfare, s. hitaM, kalyARaM, kzemaM, kuSalaM, Sreyas n., BadraM, maMgalaM, suKaM, BUti f., SivaM, susTiti f.
WELFARE: (1) kzemam, tending to w.: kzemaNkara (f. rI), B.;(2) hitam (= good: q. v.);(3) maNgalam;(4) kalyARam;(5) kuSalam;(6) Sreyas (n.).

WELFARE , s. kuSalaM, kOSalaM, kOSalyaM, kuSalatA, kalyARaM, kzemaM, kzema- kuSalaM, maNgalaM, mANgalyaM, suKaM, SuBaM, BadraM, hitaM, Sreyas n., SvaHSreyasaM, BUtiH f., susTitiH f., sTitiH f., aBIzwaM, aBIpsitaM, BavikaM, BAvukaM, BavyaM, SivaM.
Welkin, s. naBas n.; See Sky.
WELKIN: naBas (n.): v. Sky.

Well, s. vApI, kUpaH, prahiH, aMDuH, dIrGikA (‘large w(ell)’), udapAnaM; ‘covering of a w(ell)’ vi(vI)nAhaH; ‘reservoir near a w(ell)’ AhAvaH, nipAnaM, upakUpajalASayaH. 2 gupti f. a. kuSalin, svasTa, susTaSarIra, nirAmaya, nIroga, kalya; See Healthy. 2 kuSala, kzema, suKin; oft. by kuSalaM; api kuSalamasyAH prajApAlasya mAtuH (U. 4) ‘is she w(ell)’; ‘got w(ell) again’ punaH prakftisTo'Bavat, prakftimApannaH; ‘know that we are doing w(ell) in every respect’ sarvatra no vArtamavehi (R. v. 13). adv. su pr., (sukfta, sudarSana &c.); suzWu, sADa, samyak; ‘w(ell) said’ sADUkta, sUkta; ‘w(ell) off’ susTita a., vittavat susTa; ‘you might as w(ell) have kept all (fruits)’ sarvezAM rakzaRepi na tava kaSciddozo'Bavizyat. interj. bAQaM, taTA; ‘saying very w(ell)’ yujyate, bAQaM, taTeti uktvA; ‘very w(ell)’ Bavatu; ‘w(ell) then’ tena hi. 2 (As expletive) Bavatu, astu, gen. by tAvat; ‘w(ell) we go away now’ sADayAmastAvadaDunA; ‘w(ell)-behaved’ sADuSIla, suvftta; ‘w(ell)-being’ hitaM, kuSalaM; See Welfare; ‘w(ell)-born’ kulIna, satkulajAta; ‘Well-bred’, a. suvinIta; ‘w(ell)-done’ sADa sADu; ‘w(ell)-informed’ bahujYa, bahuSruta; ‘w(ell)-meaning’ sadASaya, hitabudDi; ‘w(ell)-nigh’; See Nearly; ‘w(ell)-read’ aDItin, sarvaSAstrapAraMgata, bahudfSvan; ‘Well-timed’, a. ucitAvasara; ‘Well-to-do’, a. samfdDa, ESvaryaSAlin; ‘w(ell)-wisher’ hitakAmaH, hitEzin m., priyEzin m.
WELL (subs.): (1) kUpaH, blind w.: anDakUpaH, Va.; w.-maker: kUpakft, He.;(2) anDuH (rare) Of a ship: guptiH.

WELL (adj.): (1) kuSalin (f. nI), is your pre- ceptor w.: kuSalI guruste, R. v. 4.; is Chāru- datta w.: api kuSalaM sArTavAhaputrasya, Mr. ix.; (2) susTaSarIra (f. rA: in body): v. Healthy; (3) susTa or svasTa (f. sTA), in a few days you will hear your father is w. and recovered to his health: katipayEreva divasEH punaH svAM prakftimApannaM svasTaM Srozyasi pitaram, C. v.

WELL (adv.): (1) su- in comp., w.-born: sujAta (f. tA); w.-bred: suSikzita (f. tA); w.-done: sukfta (f. tA); w.-favoured: sudarSana (f. nA); w.-formed: surUpa (f. pa); w.-known: suprasidDa (f. dDA); w.-read: svaDIta (f. tA); etc.;(2) suzWu;(3) sADu (= w.-to-do);(4) samyak. W. off: AQya (f. QyA): v. Rich, prosperous.

WELL (interj.): (1) vAQam (=very well);(2) no expr. when concessive, w., what next: tatastataH; w., be it so: Bavatu; w., I am going: mayA tAvadgamyate. Ph.: w.-done: i. e. admirable, sADu sADu; w.-affected, well-disposed: hitabudDi (mfn.) and sim. comp. s.

WELL , a. (In health) svasTaH -sTA -sTaM, susTaH &c., nirAmayaH -yA -yaM, nIrogaH -gA -gaM, see HEALTHY. — (Fortunate, happy) kuSalaH -lA -laM, kzemaH -mA -maM, hitaH -tA -taM, suKI -KinI -Ki (n); ‘Is it well?’ kiM kzemam asti.

WELL , s. (For water) kUpaH, kUpakaH, prahiH m., anDuH m., jalakUpI, kUpI, nipAnaM, udapAnaM, udakADAraH, jalADAraH, jalAtmikA, ApInaH, cUqakaH, kowwAraH; ‘wooden frame or upper part of a well,’ nemiH f., trikA; ‘cover or facing,’ vInAhaH; ‘reservoir near a well,’ AhAvaH, nipAnaM, upakUpajalASayaH; ‘well-water,’ kUpodakaM, kOpaM; ‘well-digger,’ kUpaKanitA m. (tf). — (Of a ship) guptiH f.

WELL , adv. su or ati prefixed, suzWu, sADu, samyak, yuktaM, yaTAyogyaM, BadraM, uttamarUpeRa; ‘well off,’ susTitaH -tA -taM, susTaH -sTA -sTaM; ‘well said,’ svaBihitaH -tA -taM, sUktaH -ktA -ktaM, sADvaBihitaH -tA -taM, sADUktaH &c., BadramuktaH &c.
WELL , exclam. BadraM, vAQaM, sADu, astu, Bavatu, taTeti; ‘very well,’ vAQaM, kAmaM; ‘well then,’ tadBadraM; ‘well done!’ sADu.
WELL-AFFECTED , a. suraktaH -ktA -ktaM, hitabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, suSIlaH &c.
WELL-BALANCED , a. samatolaH -lA -laM, samAnatolaH -lA -laM.
WELL-BEHAVED , a. vinItaH -tA -taM, sADuvfttiH -ttiH -tti, sADvAcAraH -rA -raM, sucaritaH -tA -taM, sadAcAraH &c., sunItaH -tA -taM.
WELL-BEING: kuSalam: v. Welfare.
WELL-BEING , s. kuSalaM, kzemaM, susTatA, susTitiH f. See WELFARE.
WELL-BORN , a. kulInaH -nA -naM, satkulInaH &c., sujanmA -nmA -nma (n), sujAtaH -tA -taM, aBijAtaH &c., sADujaH &c. See NOBLE.
WELL-BRED , a. suvinItaH -tA -taM, suSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, suSIlaH -lA -laM.
WELL-DISPOSED , a. hitabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, suSIlaH &c. See WELL-WISHER.
WELL-DOER , s. sukarmmA m. (n), sukftI m. (n). See VIRTUOUS.
WELL-DONE , a. sukftaH -tA -taM, sucaritaH &c. Exclam. sADu.
WELL-DRESSED , a. suveSaH -SA -SaM, suvezI -ziRI &c., suvezwitaH -tA -taM.
WELL-FORMED , a. surUpaH -pI -paM, surUpI -piRI &c., SudDAkAraH -rA -raM.
WELL-INFORMED: (1) bahujYa (f. jYA);(2) viSezavid (mfn.); etc.
WELL-INFORMED , a. bahujYaH -jYA -jYaM, sujYaH &c., bahuSrutaH -tA -taM.
WELL-KNIT , a. susaMhataH -tA -taM, dfQasanDiH -nDiH -nDi.
WELL-KNOWN , a. sujYAtaH -tA -taM, prasidDaH -dDA -dDaM. See NOTORIOUS.
WELL-MADE , a. surUpaH -pA -paM, surUpI -piRI &c., suGawitaH -tA -taM.
WELL-MEANING: (1) sadASaya (f. yA);(2) sadaBiprAya (f. yA); etc.
WELL-MEANING , a. sadaBiprAyaH -yA -yaM, sadASayaH &c., suSIlaH &c.
WELL-NIGH: prAyeRa: v. Nearly.
WELL-NIGH , adv. prAyas, prAyaSas. See NEARLY.
WELL-READ , a. svaDItaH -tA -taM, svaDItI -tinI -ti (n), aDItI &c., sarvvaSAstrapAragaH -gA -gaM, granTI -nTinI &c., bahujYaH &c.
WELL-SPENT , a. suvyayitaH -tA -taM; ‘time,’ satkAlakzepaH.
WELL-VERSED: (1) samyagvinIta (f. tA);(2) svaDItin (f. nI); etc.
WELL-WISHER: (1) hitEzin (f. RI);(2) hita- kAma (f. mA);(3) SuBAkANkzin (f. RI); etc.
WELL-WISHER , s. hitEzI -ziRI m. f., priyEzI -ziRI m. f., hitepsuH m. f., hitaprepsuH m. f., SreyorTI -rTinI, hitakAmaH -mA.
Welter, v. i. luW 6 P, luw 4 P; See Roll.
WELTER (v.): luWati (luW, c. 6.): v. To roll.
To WELTER , v. n. luW (c. 6. luWati -WituM), praluW. See To WALLOW.
WELTERING , part. luWan -WantI -Wat (t). See ROLLING, part.
Wen, s. mAMsArbudaM.
WEN: arvudam (?).
WEN , s. mAMsavfdDiH f., medorbudaM, galagaRqaH. See TUMOUR.
Wench, s. baMDakI, puMScalI, durvfttA. 2 kanyA, taruRI. v. i. Fornicate, q. v.
WENCH: (1) banDakI;(2) puMScalI;(3) durvfttA.
WENCH (v.): aBisarati (sf, c. 1.): v. Also to fornicate.
WENCH , s. jozA, yozitA, taruRI, kanyA, banDakI, gaRikA.
Wend, v. t. (oneʼs way) gam 1 P, cal 1 P; See Go; ‘here he w(end)s his way’ ita evABivartate.
WEND: to w. one's way: gacCati (gam, c. 1. = go, pass: q. v.) or AgacCati (= come: q. v.).
To WEND , v. n. gam, yA, i, sf, Avft, aBivft, see To GO; ‘hither he wends his way,’ ita evABivarttate.
West, s. pratIcI, paScimA, vAruRI. [West]erly, [West]ern, a. pAScAtya, pratIcya, carama, apara. 2 paScimABimuKa (KI f.). [West]wards, adv. pratIcImaBi, pratIcyaBimuKaM, paScimadiSi.
WEST: (1) paScimA dik and sim. expr.s: v. Quarter;(2) pratIcI;(3) vAruRI dik and sim. expr.s.

WEST, WESTERLY, WESTERN: (1) paScima (f. mA), in the w. sky: paScime naBasi, Ki. ix. 5.; (2) pAScAtya (f. tyA), with the w. erns whose strength lay in horse: pAScAtyEraSvasADanEH, R. iv. 62.;(3) pratIcya (f. cyA) or rarely pratIcIna (f. nA).
WEST , s. (The quarter of the sky) paScimA, paScimadiSA, paSci- madik f. (S), paScimASA, pratIcI, aparA, caramA, vAruRI, maDyaH -DyaM. The god Varuna is fabled as the Regent of the West.

WEST , WESTERLY, WESTERN, a. paScimaH -mA -maM, pratyaN -tIcI -tyak (Yc), pratIcyaH -cyA -cyaM, pratIcInaH -nA -naM, caramaH -mA -maM, aparaH -rA -raM, pAScAtyaH -tyA -tyaM. ‘Madyadesha is west of Prayāga,’ maDyadeSaH prayAgAt paScimaH; ‘as far as the western ocean,’ Apa- ScimasamudrAt. — (Facing the west) pratyaNmuKaH -KI -KaM, paScimABi- muKaH &c.
WESTWARD, -S: pratIcImaBito diSam, Mah.; and sim. exprs.
WESTWARD , adv. paScAt, pratyak, paScimadiSi, paScimatas.
Wet, a. Ardra, klinna, sikta, ukzita, unna, jalArdra. v. t. klid c., ArdrIkf 8 U, Ardrayati (D.); See Melt. s. ArdratA, temaH, kledaH. 2 durdinaM; ‘w(et)-nurse’ stanyadAyinI, DAtrI, upamAtf f.
WET (adj.): (1) Ardra (f. rdrA), the hair being wet with rain: jalArdrAlakA, Mr. v. 34.; by the w. track: ArdrapadapaMktiBiH, R. ix. 59.;(2) klinna (f. nnA), w. clothes: klinne vAsasI, Mr. v.
WET (subs.): I Wetness: ArdratA.II Rainy weather: durdinam.
WET (v.): (1) ArdrIkaroti;(2) kledayati, saM-, pra-, (c. of klid), and water does not w. him: na cEnaM kledayantyApaH, G. ii. 23.
WET , a. ArdraH -rdrA -rdraM, jalArdraH &c., klinnaH -nnA -nnaM, siktaH -ktA -ktaM, jalasiktaH &c., samukzitaH -tA -taM, anUpaH -pA -paM. See MOIST.
WET , s. ArdratA, kledaH -daM, temaH, stemaH, jalaM. See MOISTURE.
To WET , v. a. klid (c. 10. kledayati -yituM). See To MOISTEN.
WET-NURSE: stanyadAtrI DAtrI, Viv.; and sim. comp.s.
WET-NURSE , s. DAtreyI, upamAtA, upamAtrI, payaHprasraviRI, stanyadAnena pozayitrI or pAlayitrI.
Wether, s. CinnavfzaRo mezaH.
WETHER: CinnavfzaRo mezaH, and sim. comp. s.
WETHER , s. CinnavfzaRo mezaH, muzkaSUnyo mezaH.
WETNESS , s. ArdratA, klinnatA, jalArdratA, siktatA -tvaM.
WETTISH: (1) IzadArdra (f. rdrA);(2) Aklinna (f. nnA), etc.
Whale, s. timiH, timiMgilaH.
WHALE: timiH, R. xiii. 10. N. B. timiNgilaH = w. eater, a fabulous sea-monster.
WHALE , s. timiH m., timiNgilaH, timiNgilagilaH, mInaraH, samudrAruH m., makaraH, rAGavaH, vfhanmInaH.
WHALER: *timipotaH, timigrahaH.
Wharf, s. GawwaH, tarasTAnaM. [Wharf]age, s. tarapaRyaM-mUlyaM, GawwadeyaM SulkaM.
WHARF: (1) GawwaH (?);(2) umaH (?);(3) gulmaH (?).
WHARF , s. GaWWaH, umaH, tarasTAnaM, taraRasTAnaM, gulmaH.

What, pron. kiM (kaH-kA-kiM), kiM in comp.; ‘w(hat) then’ tataH kiM, kiM tarhi; ‘w(hat) is he doing now’ sa (rAjA) kimAraMBaH saMprati (U. 2); ‘w(hat) is his name’ kiMnAmAsO; ‘w(hat) else’ aTa kiM; ‘w(hat) is that to me’ kiM mama tena; ‘w(hat) though’ yadyapi. 2 yad yad. interj. kaTaM, AH, kiM, nanu. [What]ever, [What]soever, a. yad-yad. 2 yatkim, yatkiMcit; ‘to w(hosoever) person’ yasmE kasmEcitpuruzAya; yo vA ko vA BavAmyahaM, &c.

WHAT (interj.): (1) kim, w. disgrace of Droṇa: kiM kiM BAradvAjasya pariBavaH, Ve.;(2) kaTam, w. vying with me: kaTaM mayA saha sparDate, Mu.;(3) AH, w. is this also to be asked: AH idamapi kiM prazwavyaH, Pra.

WHAT (interro.): kim, w. kind, sort: kIdfSaH (SI, SaM); w. is his mother by caste: kimIyA jAtyAsya mAtA, D. viii.; w. then: tataH kim, K.; w. is (he) doing now: kiMvyApAraH samprati, Sa. vii.; w. is this trial for Rāvaṇa: daSa- kanDarasya kEzA parIkzA, B. r.; w. is his object in sending such a message: evaM sandiSatastasya ko'Bi- prAyaH, K. s.
WHAT (rel.): that which: q. v.: yad......tad.
WHAT , pron. rel. (That which) yad. — (What kind, what like, which) yAdfSaH -SI -SaM, yAdfkzaH -kzA -kzaM, yaH yA yad.

WHAT , pron. inter. kaH kA kiM, kO m. du., ke f. n. du., ke m. pl., kAH f. pl., kAni n. pl.; ‘what?’ kiM, kinnu, kimuta, kiMsvit; ‘what kind?’ kIdfSaH -SI -SaM, kIdfkzaH -kzA -kzaM, kIdfk m. f. n. (S), kimBUtaH -tA -taM; ‘on what account?’ kimarTaM; ‘what then?’ kiM tarhi, kimu; ‘what else?’ aTa kiM; ‘what do you wish to say?’ kim asi vaktukAmaH; ‘what is he doing?’ kiMvyApAraH saH; ‘what is his name?’ kinnAmaDeyaH saH; ‘to what degree?’ kimparyyantaM; ‘what is that to me?’ kiM mama tena; ‘what though?’ yadyapi.
WHAT , interj. kaTaM, kiM, kimuta, uta, ut, nanu, svit.
